Congregation of the Daughters of Saint Anne

Drawing from the Sources

Sources for knowing the charism

missionary spirit · family · the poor · young people

Rome · Via Merulana, 177

Congregation of the Daughters of Saint Anne Via Merulana, 177 — 00185 Rome

Our Religious Family, on its historical journey “toward holiness,” is preparing to celebrate the Intermediate General Assembly. With this in view, the “Study Center,” at the express request of the Superior General, Mother Virginia Sinagra, has prepared a collection of the documents of the Founders.

In searching for these authoritative sources, to be presented to the Assembly as illuminating documents for evaluating the vital process of renewal of our Family, we were guided by the orienting criterion of the four options of the 1984 General Chapter:

— missionary spirit

— family

— the poor

— young people.

We found ourselves before the inexhaustible wealth of abundant sources, varied in form and content, so we focused our attention on the documents that most vividly express the spirit of the Founders: the letters, the conferences and the “Memoirs” of Mother Rosa; personal letters and some prayers of Fr. Tornatore; circular letters of both.

The texts collected, generally excerpts, have been gathered into four chapters according to topic, with criteria and an internal logic drawn from the content of the documents themselves:

I. The collection on missionary spirit, following the chronological order of the writings of Mother Rosa and Fr. Tornatore, is divided into 3 parts: 1. “Memoirs,” letters, circular letters, conferences from 1866 to 1878

2. “Memoirs,” letters, circular letters, conferences from 1878 to 1900

3. Some writings of Fr. Tornatore

Parts 1 and 2 allow us to grasp the common thread and the development of Mother Rosa’s missionary thought and practice, with some of their characteristic elements: a. Mother Rosa’s “missionary longing”: a mystery of personal intimacy with God, but also a mystery of communion with one’s brothers and sisters, that is, love for the Father and his plan of universal salvation; love for others to the point of giving one’s life in sacrifice for all.

b. The “missionary spirituality” which, springing from the encounter with Christ Crucified, becomes a following of total dedication and of mission without borders; c. the sending “ad gentes,” readiness to go beyond one’s own borders and the second vocation of the Daughters of Saint Anne, is marked by practical criteria:

— specific formation

— inculturation

— unity in universality

— holiness and communion of life as the soul of mission; d. a missionary “pedagogy” made up of:

— accompaniment

— dialogue

— reflection in the light of Sacred Scripture

— encouragement

— witness.

Fr. Tornatore’s writings in the third part make explicit and clarify the theological and spiritual reasons for the missionary spirit of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

II. The texts on the family—conferences, letters of Mother Rosa to the Sisters and to other people outside, and a prayer of Fr. Tornatore—highlight the charismatic aspects of the Institute as an extension of the Family of the Holy Mother, and the resulting witness through concrete apostolic action for the benefit of the family.

They are therefore grouped according to these two areas, namely: a. formative documents for the internal sphere; b. documents that set out her thought on the family through her relations with Princess Emilia di Fitalia.

III. The collection on the poor was compiled according to the corresponding option, in its twofold aspect:

— the poor, persons to be served and loved “as the privileged recipients of our mission”

— the lifestyle that characterizes our way of being and of living our service to the poor.

The texts tell us clearly how Mother Rosa and the first sisters, drawn by the poor and crucified Christ and hearing the cry of the poor, went out to meet them, taking on their sufferings with motherly care. They also bring out Mother Rosa’s human and spiritual strength, Fr. Tornatore’s strong ascetical temper and his teaching influence, and the pedagogy of both in forming the sisters, who, sustained by the specific spirituality of the Family, were enabled to be “the servants of the poor” and to live the “utterly poor,” directed solely toward God and the Crucified.

IV. The texts relating to the option for young people led us to grasp:

Mother Rosa’s constant attention to the young girls she had taken in as boarders in the first communities, her educational approach toward them, her motherly concern for their present life and her provision for their future place in society.

The educational formation of the sisters, called to carry out a strong and incisive role as attentive and loving mothers toward the girls; her active charity toward young people in general.

The collection relating to the four options, compared with our sources, which are very rich in quantity and variety, is not exhaustive.

Quantity, however, given the purpose of this work, is not the only guarantee of value. Every document, every writing of the Founders carries within it the illuminating power and the warmth that release in us the vital energies of the charism. We hope for ourselves, and for all who will draw from these sources, the experience of a refreshing immersion in the spirit of the origins, the blazing power of the Holy Spirit that leads us to live faithfully the enduring values of our Religious Family and to seek new and timely ways of expressing them in the historical reality of our time.

Sr. A. Maria Eletta Convertini

Sr. A. Maria Helena Do Rozàrio

Sr. A. Elena Navarro

N.B. The documents are given in a standard critical edition, with abbreviations expanded where appropriate and punctuation and capitalization adapted to modern usage.

Memoirs 1857-1874

… Ah, my Good, you alone could tell it! Oh, you who are my Paradise! What can I do to make you known to the whole world? Oh, how many there are who do not know you, and those who have known you flee from you because they have never seen you; I would like to run everywhere and cry out aloud for everyone to come and love you…

SOURCE: MEMOIRS Fasc. I · Archive ref.: Mmm 1.1 p. 30 A.3.31

…Oh, what thirst! My Good, you quenched the thirst of a Samaritan woman: ah, let my burning thirst move you to pity! Oh, love, grant that the fire of your Love may be my only food, and that when I go to sinners to convert them my words may have such power as to convert the whole world; I suffer too much at seeing you offended! Oh, what a thirst I have, my Good, to give my life for them, so that like the martyrs I might be put on the pyre for you. Oh, endless ardor! Why shall I never come to quench my thirst?…

SOURCE: MEMOIRS Fasc. 1 · Archive ref.: Mmm 1.1 p. 38 A.3.31

…united as I was, for it was more union than meditation, one day I saw him healed: “Oh, my Love, you are healed!” A voice said to me: “You must think of taking away other scars!” “Oh, my Love, yes! My blood, to relieve you of the pains that sinners give you; and I, as the worst of all, but you teach me, and I will do everything! You know what I do for souls and I neglect nothing for their conversion; oh, what would I not do?…”

SOURCE: MEMOIRS Fasc. 1 · Archive ref.: Mmm 1.1 p. 99 A.3.31

Oh, all you souls, come! Ah, love Jesus, do not offend him! By the love you bear your creatures, teach me how I must do to make you known to everyone. A fire so vehement that I could resist no longer: I would have run through all the streets crying out to them to love Jesus! I threw myself face down on the ground and begged the Eternal Father with all my strength to let me die a martyr to save the souls redeemed by Him. Am I not your instrument, which you toss here and there as you please? Then once and for all let this blood be shed to the last drop to satisfy your justice (…) My Love, consume me on the Altar of Sacrifice…

SOURCE: MEMOIRS · Archive ref.: Mmm 1.1 p. 119-120 A.3.31

To Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 1867 (?)

Courage, my daughter, show yourself a generous daughter of your Mother, our Saint Anne, a daughter detached from everything, a daughter who seeks nothing but the interest, the pleasure and the glory of her Mother, the great Saint, who can accept as daughters only generous hearts, ready for love of her to go and to stay anywhere and to suffer everything for Jesus.

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF (n. 26) A.2.14

To Sr. A. Caterina Rapallino and to the Sisters of Piacenza, from Cento, 18.2.1867

…Look at Peter: “Come”, the Master said to him, and he, without thinking that he had a family and other things, ran at once; so it happened to all those who followed the Saviour. Certainly this Master did not go for walks or after pleasures, but was ready to leap hedges and climb through forests, heeding nothing, neither food nor clothing, but only the track of the lost sheep; and all these apostles went together with Jesus to suffer hunger and thirst and, to say it all in one word, suffering was their refreshment. Behold, whoever wants to follow me, says the Master (showing us a Cross), let him take up his Cross and follow me…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF — 1867 A.2.14

To the Sisters of Sampierdarena, 25.2.1871

…So, courage! The Holy Pope Pius IX told me: we shall be like so many apostles, our Institute will spread to all parts of the world. How then can I fear, having this before my eyes? I pray that God may send us a little providence, but for nothing else. At Piacenza we go to assist the sick with everyone's applause, the Bishop blesses us, and even the worst listen to us, and all this by the mercy of God… We are sailing under full sail without my doing anything. Yes, I will always say it and can confirm it: I have done nothing for this Work. The Lord has done everything…

SOURCE: CONFERENCE VIII (p. 53-54) Archive ref.: MmC 1.1 A.3.36

To Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, from Rome, 2.6.1871

I hope you will have received all our letters, my blessed little daughter. If prayers do not miraculously obtain what we want, this horizon seems very dark for us; but the right hand of our Eternal Father can dispel everything in an instant, and the Daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, can enjoy the most beautiful light there is in all Catholicism and carry it to shine in the most idolatrous lands, and plant there the standard of Saint Anne. I am pleased to hear the good news you give me of the little girls: I bless God for it, praying him to continue pouring out on them the dew of his mercies…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 1871 A.2.14

To the Sisters of Ferrara, 16.3.1872

… Sisters, you are the seeds of our Institute. On you, the first, depends the good success of the others…

So in the street and with the sick you must observe your Rules as if you had them in your pocket, for everyone looks at you and watches you; and if you do as I tell you, you will be that seed which will sprout in this House, which in the course of time will become a great foundation, and God will bless your labors and you will find yourselves crowned with a most resplendent crown…

SOURCE: CONFERENCE XI (p. 25.27) Archive ref.: MmC 1.1 A.3.36

To the Sisters of Piacenza, 25.5.1872

… We have left the world and consequently everything; and what is the use of wearing ourselves out at the bedsides of the sick, and of the teachers exhausting their lungs over the girls, if then for some worthless rag spoiled we must lose the crown that has been prepared for us? (…) You see, at Ferrara we have more than 140 girls, all taken out of sin; so it is no wonder if this work is assailed; never in the world has a work been seen to flourish so quickly as this one. Every day there are new crosses, but I keep saying: these are the foundations that make the walls of our House, of our Institute, more solid; I am not dismayed, rather I rejoice… Ah, how much you must thank God for having led you here and gathered you within his walls, in the work of Saint Anne, which can never collapse and will last eternally for all ages of ages.

SOURCE: CONFERENCE XXI (153, 161.162) Archive ref.: MmC 1.1 A.3.36

To the Sisters of Piacenza, 21.7.1872

…The Daughter of Saint Anne must be, as our Father Pius IX told me, “an apostle who preaches the faith by her good actions and good example: to those who are religious, to increase them ever more in their fervor; to those who are not religious, to draw them to devotion or at least to make them Christians”…

SOURCE: CONFERENCE XXV (p. 200) Archive ref.: MmC 1.1 A.3.36

To Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, 4.1.1873

Just a hurried line to tell you that everything you are doing is fine. As for Sr. A. Adelaide, tell her to take courage, for I want her to get well so that she can come and work with me. Faith, faith; let her remember what she promised me: that she would get well and, at my call, be ready to work; the harvest is great, workers are needed…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 1873 A.2.14

To the Sisters — 1875

…At present the Institute numbers twenty-three houses and three hundred sisters; in the year just ended, 1874, six houses were founded, and in the year 1875, barely begun, there are already requests.

To whom, sisters, do we owe so rapid a spread of the Institute, in the few years since it was born? Certainly to the mercy of the Heavenly Father, who has been pleased to bless it. In general the sisters are animated by the spirit of their vocation; they keep before their eyes the end for which the Lord raised them to the great nobility of being daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, the end namely of consecrating their whole life to blessing him, thanking him and praising him for all the wonders worked in their Holy Mother, and for the greatest of all, that of having made her Mother of the Immaculate, his Mother Mary Most Holy, and of imitating her in all her virtues, which are taught us by our Holy Rules.

Above all three points serve to attain the aforesaid end: first, punctuality in rising, so that as soon as they hear the five o'clock bell they get up at once, without letting even a moment pass; second, that at half past five they are all already in the Chapel to begin the meditation…

SOURCE: Circular letter 1875 Archive ref.: NO 75 B.1.63

To Sr. A. Benedetta Carrega, 23.2.1875, from Piacenza

…my dear little daughter, always be cheerful; remember that I am always yours, and I often tell my Angel to go and guard you and always stay close to you, so that by your good example you may edify everyone; and in doing so you will be able to convert the whole world, and whoever is near you will love God, our only Good. Goodbye, many greetings to your papa…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIB.C. A.2.16

To the Sisters [1876]

Behold, sisters, the year just ended was also full of heavenly blessings for our poor Institute.

The Heavenly Father, who planted it in the garden of his Church, looks upon it with an eye of special predilection: he has increased its houses and multiplied its members.

In the past year 9 new houses were opened and 46 sisters received the habit; with the spread of the houses and the increase of the sisters he has been pleased to strengthen it ever more firmly in the spirit of its vocation.

The Lord raised up our Institute to be the family of the glorious Saint Anne, august Mother of Mary Immaculate, a family in which the great Saint would be honored, loved and imitated. And in general the sisters respond to this purpose. They imitate the life their Mother led on this earth for the good of her neighbor.

The service they render to the sick, both in hospitals and in homes, is done with a spirit of faith and a love of sacrifice that clearly show they keep in mind the divine words of Jesus Christ, who assures us that the care given to the sick for love of him he regards as done to himself. No less watchful is the care of those employed in teaching to imitate the piety of our Holy Mother. They spend on it all the talent they have received from the Lord, so that their pupils may be good before God and before men; they bring them up dear to Jesus Christ, and such as to become the consolation of their families. A sign of this spirit of their vocation which animates them is that, by God's goodness, they generally enjoy the goodwill of the cities and towns where they work. Our Bishops, in whose dioceses we have houses, have given open testimony of this goodwill. They have written the most cordial and expressive letters of recommendation, in which the sisters are highly praised for their zeal and for their wise and modest conduct, by which they edify their people (…) Not only are the Bishops pleased with us, but we are also respected and honored by the civil authorities. But what crowns our joy is the love that the Vicar of Jesus Christ bears our poor Institute (…)

Behold, sisters: the lovableness of our Holy Mother, which drew to her the affection of the heart of God, of the divine heart of Jesus and of Mary, is poured out upon us and makes us objects of affection to heaven and to all the noblest creatures on earth; but the signs of affection of the Heavenly Father and of the Holy Mother would not have been complete if tribulations had not been mingled with the consolations that accompanied our family in the past year.

Yes, crosses, which are the mark of God's chosen works, were not lacking to us; two in particular we felt keenly, namely the taking from us of its most zealous sisters, the most tireless in spreading the Institute and increasing its glory: you already understand that we mourn the loss of Sister Anna Vincenza and Sister Anna Francesca. Yes, we can bear witness that the love they had for increasing the splendor of their Holy Mother was what made them two victims and sacrificed them for the good of her family; but the Lord has willed it so: may his adorable will always be done.

In so great a loss, however, we have reason for consolation, and the reason is that the example they have left us will spur us to imitate them, and not to be content until we reach the point of being able to say: the love we have had for our God, for the glory of the Holy Mother and for the spread of her Institute has taken our life. What gratitude does God ask of us for the favors with which he has filled us in the year now ended? He wants a deep sense of humility, by which we confess that we have not deserved them… and which makes us confess before his Divine Majesty that we are his unprofitable servants…

The second thing he wants of us is that we be attentive to the observance of the Rules… in particular to punctuality in rising… rising is the first sacrifice he asks of us in the day: if this sacrifice is made with the promptness he requires, then it earns us a special grace to make our holy meditation well, and on meditation well made depends our spiritual progress (…)

If the Institute holds firm to these cardinal points of the rule, it will be a solid building that will not fear the assaults of its enemies, whether of the world or the demons of hell; it will be a joy to the Holy Mother, who will be glorified, loved and imitated in it by her daughters; and they will then merit, at the end of their days, the crown of glory the Lord holds ready for those who serve him with a true heart.

SOURCE: CIRCULAR LETTER 1876 Archive ref.: IIC 76 B.1.63

To Sr. A. Gesuina Moroni, 4.1.1876, from Piacenza

I am truly glad of the good news you give me. Yesterday I spoke with the Priest who came from Rocca: what a good person! I was very pleased and hope you will soon be there and able to do good. Yes, in the summer someone from here will be able to come; courage, my little daughter, for it is time to work and to carry out great missions, to win souls for God! Too many are plunging into the abyss of hell. Courage, blood for blood: Jesus on the cross is all torn, and so are we, isn't that so? Goodbye, for I am so busy that I really do not know what to do. Goodbye, my dear, greet everyone for me, and receive a thousand good wishes from your affectionate M. R.

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 76 A.2.14

To Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, 6.1.1877, from Rome

Do not be daunted by the distance; no, you must instead do everything so that I can send two more at once, and you will teach them how they must do… so we are agreed: you show at once that two more are needed, and I will send them to you at once. Send me the travel itinerary so that I can give it to them; for the rest, be at peace, for you will be with me forever…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 77 A.2.14

To Sr. A. Costanza Cenni, 8.2.1877, from Rome

My little daughter: I feel the sorrow you have at losing an earthly mother. Listen: I left Genoa, where I was told plainly that my father had only a few days to live; and indeed, when I reached Rome, which I did in one stretch, he died! The work required that I leave, and I did so at once; and the same with my son and Mother, my Brother — in short, my little daughter, sacrifice is very pleasing to God, and the Lord our Master said to Peter: leave father and mother and follow me; or again, to one who said, I am going to bury, the Lord answered: let the dead bury the dead, and he did not allow it. So what does this mean? That once we have given ourselves to him he does not want us to have any more dealings with earthly things, but to raise our mind to him alone; he becomes jealous. Courage, pray, and I would like to say nothing more — still a million things, but if you only knew that I have not a free breath and that I am stealing this quarter of an hour for you; so I would like these words of mine to suit you and that you draw true fruit from them.

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 1877 A.2.14

To Sr. A. Celsa Speranza, 6.7.1877, from Piacenza

Just one line because I am in a hurry: courage, for whoever sows well will reap a great harvest; so to sow one must work and toil with the sweat of one's brow, because the soil is barren and many fields are untilled; what labor!! Be strong in the battles! Goodbye, thank you for the holy picture.

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MI C.S (5) A.2.16

To Sr. A. Irene Carmeli, 27.4.1877, from Naples

Abraham's sacrifice made him Father of the Living; so our sacrifice this time of not being able to see each other will mean that the first time we meet we shall stay long together and gather all the time to pour ourselves out in words all of God, and we shall speak of what the soul needs for its nourishment. Oh, blessed day when I shall press my dear little daughter to my heart! Oh, how many, my God, will be the expressions of affection towards you in that moment! What shall we be able to say? Both of us back from work and resting, always in the field so as to be ready to undertake new battles and labors without equal, speaking of you, whom I promise to call a beautiful and infinite love who have stolen everything from us and left us alone, exiles in the barren land where so few know the language of your Love. Oh, little daughter, when shall I see you all fire, burning in these flames of love! Listen: the house in this city is now being opened; so think of helping these poor sisters by sending them whatever you have to spare, do you understand? My God, we have not yet been able to find anything; what a worry: there is rent to pay, and you know what burdens I carry on my shoulders; for charity's sake, my little daughter, send us something…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 1877 A.1.14

To Sr. A. Fiorenza Riboldi, 8.7.1877, from Piacenza

None of your suppositions are true — my God! — listen, you see it is quite the opposite, because when a Superior orders a sister to go and work in some house, it means she has placed her trust in her and holds her to be her good little daughter. If it were otherwise she would not send her to the vineyard to work and sow fine wheat, and so straighten certain plants which, having been left untended, need to be straightened; so set to work and try to bring it about that from being sick they become healthy and turn into so many little angels, who are to make a fine crown for the Lord. Oh, blessed are you, who have been placed in an untended garden! Blessed! For your labors will rise to heaven and the blessed there will gather them; you will find them all around your head like a most beautiful garland of fragrant lilies. Oh, whoever knows how to work well and spend herself for Jesus, blessed is she! Soul of the Lord, work without ceasing! What joy! Keep your eyes fixed on Heaven and work, work until the crows are turned into lambs!!…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 1877 A.2.14

To the Sisters (1878)

Oh, how good is the God of Israel! So we have every reason to exclaim, seeing the great mercies with which he has filled us this year too.

Yes, his most merciful eyes were continually open upon our poor Institute. The Daughter of Saint Anne no longer lives for herself but for her Institute; so she takes account of its blessings, those the Lord poured out upon the Family of the Holy Mother.

The chief blessing, to be counted before all others, is that of having granted the sisters in general the grace of observance.

Among the virtues I will touch only on holy indifference, which is as it were the uniform of the Daughters of Saint Anne, keeping them detached from everything so as to be ready for any country to which obedience may wish to send them: yes, to our heart's great joy we must say that in general none ever made excuses for not leaving the house where she lived to go to the one to which we assigned her. Admirable too was the ready spirit with which they devoted themselves to the care of the sick and the education of girls… (…) The relations our Institute maintains with outsiders are consoling in every respect.

And first of all, how the Holy Father continues in his predilection for us!!! Among the many proofs he has given of this special affection, an outstanding one is what we received most recently: he deigned to buy us a fine house in Rome, at the place called the Parrocchietta, where a school of ours is flourishing…

And what calls we have received to open new houses! So many that this year eleven houses were opened. The numerous vocations bear witness to the esteem of the people in general; indeed this year 82 sisters received the habit.

This esteem we enjoy among people of the world we must value only as a sign that our Institute is of spiritual and temporal benefit to the Church, and so that the Lord is glorified through us, as we correspond to the proximate end for which he placed us in his Church, which is to honor and to make everyone honor the august and glorious Mother of the Immaculate, our Mother Saint Anne. At the same time it must make us reflect that it is the protection of the Holy Mother over us that draws all these blessings upon us from heaven, and it must kindle in us ever more a holy, fervent and filial affection for this our most exalted and most tender Mother, who for us is the channel through which all graces come to us from heaven by the hands of Mary, her Immaculate Daughter…

SOURCE: Circular letter 1878 by M. Rosa and P.G. B. Tornatore Archive ref.: IIC 78.1 B.1.63

To Sr. A. Irene Carmeli

…little daughter, the first holiness lies in obeying…

…let us obey blindly: look, I am dying with the desire to go to America, but my Superiors said no; oh, I repeat: no, no; if we want love we must obey. Let them call me ignorant, stupid, foolish; oh, happy am I if they give me these titles for having obeyed…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 78 A.2.14

Daughters, stand firm in the promises you have made to the Lord; strive day by day to respond ever more to your vocation. Dear daughters, we shall be far apart in body, but in the heart of Jesus we shall be united in spirit forever. I recommend to you the exact observance of our Holy Rules; be ready to die rather than fail in our Constitutions. Love the Holy Rules and you will be saints. Daughters, the saints became saints because they loved the cross and held it as a great treasure; they embraced it tightly (…) as Jesus did (…) Over there you will find many hardships, and a great cross awaits you, but do not be afraid. Be faithful to the Cross of Jesus, on which he breathed out his most holy life… For charity's sake, daughters, listen to that divine voice by which the Lord will make you hear what he wants of you. Be ready to receive that Cross, that self-denial, that renunciation of your own will, all that Jesus will make you suffer for love of him. In doing so you will return to the feet of Jesus comforted, full of courage to serve him with greater perfection.

Beloved daughters, I shall always be with you — and you will be dearer to me than all my other daughters, and we shall always see one another in the heart of Jesus…

SOURCE: CONFERENCE undated Archive ref.: MmCx-4 A.3.36

To Sr. A. Guglielmina Merli, 22.11.1878, from Piacenza

From your letter I learn of the sister's poor health; I am very sorry about it. As for sending her to Sermoneta, I can assure you it would only put her at risk, and would surely make her die on the way, since it is a place one has to reach on horseback… enough; you tell me you are afraid of yourself: it is good always to distrust ourselves so as to belong wholly to Jesus! So be at peace. Oh, if you had seen yesterday the fine expedition of 16 sisters, all of long standing in their vocation and so full of the spirit of sacrifice that they edified everyone! The Bishop came twice to greet them, and so did all their relatives; but with what courage they answered! The Holy Father sent them his Holy Blessing; in short, they made me envious. The Superior is Sr. A. Giuseppa, the one who was appointed Visitor and was at Pistoia, who has twelve and a half years of vocation, and the others too; what a fine spirit! Let us bless God for it! Pray that they may have a good voyage… as it is very long, 36 days…

SOURCE: LETTERS · Archive ref.: MIF 78 A.2.14

To Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni — Bolivia, 13.12.1878, from Piacenza

Just a line to tell you that I have always received your letters along the journey; the last is from Spain, where you tell me you suffered a good deal, but that you were well and are cheerful and content, and that you have very great courage. Oh yes, this is all God's work: dear Jesus has given you his gifts of strength and courage in the labors of so long a journey. I pray much for it, and every morning — you will tell the dear sisters — I always offer the Lord your sixteen hearts together with your will, so that God the Father may do with them what he thinks best and give you strength, courage and living faith to do everything for him alone, wanting nothing for the earth; for oh, how sweet it is to suffer for Jesus! How many times I have asked to be among you, but I am not worthy; my wickedness keeps me from running swiftly to the summit of dear Mount Tabor, and I must always stay at the foot of Golgotha, waiting for the day of my departure to climb Calvary; it is only there that the Beloved is found. But, my dear daughters, I am barely at the foot of this mountain, eager to climb; but who, who stands in the way is the barrier of my sins: it has dug itself in, and I struggle but cannot climb. Oh, what sorrow!!! Pray and say every day: “Hear her and give her what she asks of you.” Oh, I would like to see you, ah!!!, in the gentle wards, beside the bed of Jesus, now dressing his wounds, now doing what he needs! And so he gives your hearts those sweet throbs of love; every morning I tell him to consume you in himself. Oh, sweet Love! Consume my dear creatures and keep all 16 of them with me in your [Heart] always, for an eternity; I hope that solely by the pure mercy of God I may go there. I await your letters anxiously; I assure you I count the days and the hours; and I have written this so that you may have my news before I have to answer yours, which you will send me from La Paz. Courage, and I am always with you; in the Novena of the Child Jesus I will try to press him into your heart, as I am sure you will do the same for me. Goodbye, the Lord bless you, and always believe me yours…

To the Sisters, 1.1.1879, from Piacenza

The year now ending, 1878, sets before our eyes, O dearest sisters and daughters, the blessings we have received from the Lord in its course. Oh, how numerous and great they are! One, and the most outstanding, is the benevolence with which the Vicar [of Christ], the Supreme Pontiff happily reigning, Leo XIII, regards our Institute. Not only has he confirmed the gift of the House and vineyard of the Parrocchietta, which the late Holy Father of holy memory made us at the end of his days, but at his own expense he had the house restored. We know that he greatly rejoices to see how quickly our Institute is spreading. This concern of the Vicar of Jesus Christ for the growth of our Institute assures us that God takes pleasure in it. The Bishops of the various dioceses in which we have houses, too, show themselves very satisfied with the services we perform there. We also win the goodwill of the people among whom we work. We had a proof of this goodwill from the people of Maratea, who, when a government Commissioner high-handedly tried to send our teachers away, opposed him en masse and with all the power in their hands. But to what, dearest sisters and daughters, must we attribute so many blessings from heaven? To the prayers that our Holy Mother continually offers before the Throne of the Lord. It is to her prayers that we must attribute the rapid spread of the Institute: in this year now closing we have opened eleven houses, among which special mention is due to the one we founded in the new world, I mean in South America, where sixteen of our sisters have gone to care for two hospitals in the city of La Paz. Ninety sisters received the habit this year. So, dearest sisters and daughters, many and great are the blessings that call for our gratitude to the Lord who deigned to bestow them on us.

But in general we have reason to rejoice that in the houses of our Institute, in gratitude to God for so many and such great blessings received from him, the fragrant sacrifice of the observance of the Holy Rules is offered; we are, however, compelled to deplore the lapses of some sisters. In the first place, deplorable is the spirit of those superiors who show little affection for the Mother [House], which is as it were the center and the heart of the Institute. These unhappy Superiors do not reflect that, just as a ray cut off from its center dies out and a limb cut off from the heart dies, so they are dead limbs (…) The Mother House is like the heart of the Institute; so just as the limbs of the body are all solicitude that the heart may be strong, since life depends on it, so all good superiors are anxious that the Mother House be helped and be able to receive many postulants (…) While, then, on the one hand we are grateful to those good Superiors who show themselves true daughters of the Holy Mother and zealous for the growth of her family, we urge those lacking in zeal and love to imitate their example. (…)

To the sisters in general we recommend first of all diligence in being punctual for the exercises of piety — meditation, Mass, Communion, thanksgiving, prayers, chaplet, examen, Holy Rosary — punctuality at community acts, punctuality in rising, at breakfast, dinner, supper and recreation. In the second place we recommend that they be industrious, carrying out well the duties entrusted to them. In the third place we recommend that they see in their superiors the person of Jesus Christ, and therefore love, respect and obey them (…) This, dearest sisters and daughters, is what the Lord wants of us, so that we may show ourselves grateful for the blessings God has granted us in the year just ended and be ready to receive new ones, and so have the consolation of seeing our Company flourish for the glory of God and of the Holy Mother…

I have received the Superior's letter and hear that some of you have suffered, some more, some less; the last one I had, a few days ago, was from Rio de Janeiro, so by now you will be at your destination, all full of good will to edify those poor people and so the whole city of La Paz, which will be watching your actions with a thousand eyes. I already wrote you another letter shortly after your departure, so that you would find news of me, which will surely have been dear to you, as yours are dear to me; I ardently long to receive the one that tells me: “Here we are, we have arrived!”

Oh, let us do everything for the glory of God and the good of our neighbor; let us see in those dear sick people the person of our Lord, our dear Redeemer (…) oh, infinite sweetness! Without him there is nothing good or beautiful; with him we have everything, we lack nothing (…).

God bless you; and always think of your poor Mother, whom you left not to be separated but to be ever more united in mind and heart…

To the Sisters, 31.1.1880, from Rome

Behold, our Institute, the family of the august and glorious Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate, our mother, has entered the fourteenth year of its existence (…) Yes, daughters, very many are the divine mercies with which the year 1879 was filled. The greatest, the most deeply felt and splendid, is that Holy Church, through her Vicar now reigning, Leo XIII, has definitively recognized our family as a religious family, which is to say as a Family of God (…) Since then the goodwill of the people towards us, who bear the most noble name of Daughters of Saint Anne, is seen to grow ever greater (…) A clear proof of this goodwill is the many requests received for the founding of houses in various places.

The foundations decided on number 19, nine of which have already been opened, and the other ten will open shortly. Among these new Houses, one has been founded in America, in Bolivia, beside the one already there. In it some 80 girls are being brought up in religion. Negotiations are under way to found three more houses, likewise there in America, in three different cities, for which 40 Sisters would be called.

This eagerness to have our sisters arises from seeing the fine results obtained by the people who have them, both in Hospitals and in Schools (…)

The number of those who received the habit was 57, a number much lower than that of '78; but the cause was not a shortage of postulants asking to wear the habit of the Holy Mother, but that, owing to the critical times we are living in, they were not able to bring the dowry that is required, little as it is. On the other hand, the Mother House, given the hardship of the times, has not been able to open its arms to receive them without a dowry. And here comes the point to be especially recommended to Superiors: economy, so that after maintaining and clothing the sisters they may send the surplus to the Mother House. To this they are bound by love, by vow and by justice. By love, they must know that the fruitfulness of the Institute depends on two points: the first is that the Lord should call many, even with a very small dowry or none at all. Now the first point was not lacking this year, for the requests were very many; but the Mother House lacked the means to receive them without a dowry. And on whom does it depend that the Mother House should have these means? It depends precisely on the economy practiced by the Superiors. It is consoling to say that many true daughters of the Holy Mother, eager to see her family spread throughout the world, are most careful to account for every last cent, as the saying goes, so as to have a surplus to send to the Mother House, knowing that on its well-being depends the well-being of the whole Institute. The Mother House is the heart of the Institute; if the Heart is healthy and full of life, the limbs of the other Houses too are healthy and strong. But the Holy Mother does not receive this joy from all…

To the Sisters, 8.1.1881, from Piacenza

Casting our eyes, dearest daughters, over the whole of this year eighteen hundred and eighty… we have reason to exclaim with the holy Prophet: O Lord my God, I will sing your divine mercies forever. The most outstanding mercy is that so many of our sisters have been crowned with the crown of eternal happiness (…) they died a death that leaves nothing to be desired, the best possible to assure us that they are in heaven enjoying God in the company of the Holy Mother. Not only the good but even the wicked have been compelled to pay homage to their charity, which, in imitation of their Divine Master, drove them to sacrifice their bodily life to relieve their neighbor. To their motherly charity towards the sick Jesus Christ granted the consolation of bringing many back to his loving Divine Heart, after long years in which, abandoning him, they had given themselves to the devil and were on the point of being damned forever. Among these converted sinners there was also a Protestant heretic, cared for by our sisters at the end of his life. Seeing the truly Christian charity with which they nursed him night and day, he recognized that the Roman Church, which can inspire so disinterested a love of neighbor, could only be the one Church of Jesus Christ; and so, moved by divine grace… he was converted (…) Ah, sisters, with how many souls the charity of the Institute has crowned the throne of the Holy Mother and peopled holy paradise! But hold firmly, sisters, that all this spiritual fruitfulness which God grants is the reward of the filial love we bear the Holy Mother, the august and venerable Mother of the Immaculate. She lives in her true daughters, and so her true daughters are able to keep their hearts free from attachment to possessions, pleasures and honors, so that, inflamed by the holy love of God, they may be holy themselves and sanctify their neighbor. Therefore the longing to become true and mature Daughters of our Holy Mother must always be alive, honoring her with all the daily devotions the Institute has established for this purpose, and imitating her by faithful observance of the Holy Rules.

It is their uniform as daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of Mary, that makes them objects of admiration and veneration in the eyes of the people, so that requests for new houses come from all sides. This year twelve new ones were opened; but how many more were the requests that could not be accepted for lack of members! It is true that this year we clothed a hundred postulants, yet in view of the many houses they are few…

(…) Courage, for it is time to work and to suffer so as one day to have the good fortune of being all held close to dear Jesus; love much and you will be blessed. (Postscript to Sr. A. Giuseppa Troni — Bolivia)

To the Sisters [1884]

Let us never forget, dearest daughters, that the end for which the Heavenly Father planted the Institute in the garden of his Church is that the august and venerated Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate, may be honored in a most singular way by those who are called by her and bear the most noble name of her Daughters. (…)

Now we come to give you news of all the notable events that took place in the Institute in the course of the year. 1st On 23 May the first stone was solemnly laid of the Church being built beside the Generalate House in Rome (…)

2nd This year 16 houses were opened and two expeditions were made to America. The first expedition took place on 1 October. Ten sisters left Italy for those remote regions, called by Señor Arce to found a new Hospital at Potosí, a city not very far from Sucre; joyful and content, they bade a last farewell to the Mother House to go in search of souls and people paradise. The second took place on 15 December. Six sisters went to Oruro, another city of Bolivia, to open a new Hospital. The calls that had to be refused for lack of personnel were countless. Let us pray, then, to the Holy Mother that the number of postulants may multiply, so that we may accept the many calls to open new houses.

3rd The arrival of the American [sisters] filled all the sisters of the Mother House with the greatest consolation. After four months of long waiting they finally arrived on 18 November. As soon as the telegram announcing their arrival at Genoa was received, in spite of the poor health the Mother was in, she wanted to go there at once, but, held back almost by force, she anxiously awaited the longed-for day (…) We also make known to all Superiors and Sisters that Sr. A. Camilla Valentini, Superior of Sucre, has been elected Provincial and Visitor of Bolivia. Therefore whatever she does and arranges, whether for the acceptance of postulants or for the transfer of sisters, and also in deciding to accept new houses and to sign contracts, will be fully approved and accepted by us. Notice of this has been given by special letters to the Bishops of Bolivia.

It is further desired that in America the prayers, the chapter and everything our rule prescribes be carried out one day in Italian and one day in Spanish (…)

We can explain the delay of this Circular of ours in a few words. In the last days of December the Holy Mother was pleased to favor this Generalate House with no small number of Princes of Holy Church and a further number of Archbishops and Bishops with their retinues. We could not say no, because their insistent requests for lodging were joined by the wish of the Supreme Pontiff; and so only now are we free, and after attending to other very important matters, we are seeing to sending you this Circular of ours for this year, because, as you well know, the 6th year since the General Chapter has ended, and at the end of this year, God willing, I shall have the consolation of seeing all the Superiors around me once more, except you, my dearest American daughters. Matters concerning our poor Institute will be dealt with, to give it greater spiritual growth.

Dear daughters, let us unite in holy Observance, the lapses from which in America we deplore with the greatest sorrow, since serious harm and real scandals result from them. Our heart breaks with grief to think that you went to those regions intending to bring to those poor souls the word of God, the teaching of our Holy Catholic, Apostolic and Roman Church, catechizing the peoples so that they might leave sin and lead the life of good Christians. Have you completely forgotten these resolutions you made? I receive letters in which you tell me: “Ah, where have we come to! What barbarous lands! Wicked people without Religion. We have to suffer, because wherever we turn our eyes we see nothing but wickedness.” Well then: before you left I told you countless times that it was a new grace you were receiving from God in feeling inspired for the New Mission; and when it was said, “Over there you will find nothing but brutes,” I answered you: “Take care not to go there and be converted yourselves instead of converting others…” Horror! If I had to repeat not only the paragraph above, where you made ardent resolutions, but even oaths before God, and then… and then…

[In the] first place, poverty has been lost (…) Moreover, forgetful of the prohibition of the Holy Rules (…) Superiors, examine your consciences (…) You subjects, remember that for promises made to God and not kept you must give, and will give, a very strict account (…) I want to hope that from now on you will open your eyes more, removing all those abuses that go against holy Poverty and the observance of the Holy Rules; and then I assure you that your Houses will flourish again, and the blessed God will protect your Religious Family in a singular way and pour out most abundant graces upon you. Then I shall be able to say at the foot of my Crucifix: “The untended tree which until today has borne no fruit pleasing to your heart, behold it all in blossom to produce new fruits, so as to be accepted and blessed by You, my God.”

Receive an embrace at the foot of the Cross, where I am, and I ask an ample blessing, and I am your most affectionate M. Rosa Gattorno. (…) The novices clothed in 1887 numbered 157; the houses opened numbered [?], two of them in America.

It is they [who go] to work in foreign lands. Here they are, ready for sacrifice. They are not attached to the ownership of their houses, but even at the cost of their health they hasten wherever obedience calls them. In Africa, in less than a month, that Superior divided up all the sisters to take on new houses among those Abyssinians who do not know God and learn only from the poor Daughters of Saint Anne to love the One who is all our consolation. And not content with sending the sisters, this creature herself hastens wherever the greater good of those poor wretches requires. In the midst of so many sorrows, yes, this is a support that keeps us alive (…)

Allow us to make known to you another affliction of ours. For some years the spirit of self-preservation has entered our poor Institute: the Devil has cleverly entered your feelings, persuading you that you do it for fear of falling ill and then being no longer fit to work, and so a burden to the Institute. Horror! The good sick sisters are our jewels. We will not go on to tell you all the other reports that unfortunately are related and written to us.

(…) So for you sacrifice does not exist. Did you become sisters to be comfortably settled, or to respond to your vocation by having a nest of peace, a sure road that leads you to the desired Goal? That Goal, however, is gained only by sacrifice, by self-denial, and is reached only by the Religious who thinks solely of increasing her talents so as one day to have a place nearer to Jesus and enjoy him the more in the Homeland of the Holy Souls.

Strive, dear daughters, to imitate the virtues of the Holy Mother of the Immaculate Virgin Mary (…) and, holding fast to the Crucified, say: “You alone for all; in You I want to live and to be wholly consumed by Your love”… As this time we must speak to You Superiors alone, allow us to give vent to our heart, oppressed as never before by many breaches of observance which immensely embitter the Heart of God. We find no words that can express to you our great sorrow and what we feel! We do not mean that among the great number we do not have daughters who carry out their office so well that they are intent on nothing but observance and the greater good of their Sisters. These, though few in number, are a relief, and we are comforted by the thought that their prayers and the blessings God will pour out on their Houses are what upholds the great edifice of the Lord. No thought is ever given to the good of the poor Sisters entrusted to them, as is confirmed to us by the neglect of the exercises of piety, and no thought is ever given to providing a word of comfort for their souls, such as the conferences of some good Priest, or the Holy Exercises once a year. Oh, and these! How we must stop here to make you see how deplorable your way of acting is! If you can, you do everything to avoid them; if corrected by Us and by the Confessors themselves, instead of ten days you get as far as doing half, perhaps even three days, and then no more attention is paid to them.

To the Sisters of Ferrara, 1.6.1872

… What I have observed with sorrow is that charity is not observed in all our poor houses as I would wish, so today I will speak to you on this point, because we more than other religious must practice this virtue, since we always find ourselves with occasions to exercise it. First of all, if we want to have charity towards outsiders, we must first exercise it among ourselves, one with another, bearing with one another, pleasing everyone, relieving whichever of us we see distressed. We must see that the end of each of our actions is God and not our own satisfaction; try to be prompt and watchful, to take the lowest places; those actions which God gives us the grace to see despised by men, we must rejoice in them, for the more they are scorned and mocked by men, the more beautiful they will be in God's eyes. Look purely at the glory of God alone and make it the basis of our every action. The Saints knew that by that humiliation they pleased God, and they embraced it at once, because they knew they were giving pleasure and glory to God. Mortification of ourselves pleases God; we must mortify our interior and exterior senses. Let us take the exterior ones, which are: abstaining from eating and drinking, from eating things pleasant to our palate, not eating between meals; subjecting our body to the rigors of the seasons; caring for the sick, for all the Saints have had to pass by this road.

I go into the kitchen, for example, I see a piece of bread, I feel like taking it; I give in to the senses, I take it and put it in my mouth. At that moment a girl or a sister passes by, sees it and is scandalized; and so this sister has done two wrongs, one for not having been able to mortify herself, the other for the scandal she has given. So mortify yourselves even in ordinary matters of eating and say: Lord, I offer this to you; and do as the Saints did, who found ways of mortifying themselves in everything; it was these abstinences that brought them to union with God, to those perfect unions that united their souls to God; so too mortify yourselves in words, by keeping silence…

Then we have the third point, which is the consideration of ourselves. What are we? A handful of dust. The more graces God gives us, the more we know what we are and humble ourselves, if these graces are genuine and really come to us from God. For example, today God grants us a great grace, he makes us know the immensity of his greatness, so that the creature humbles herself, makes herself a toad, recognizes herself as the most abject creature on this earth; and this way of acting makes her pleasing before God, and if she had to undergo a million humiliations before everyone, she goes to meet them cheerfully, because she feels a great hunger for them, and in this way she is truly safe. Instead, when [the saints] are praised, they fear falling into pride and losing God, because they know that if God withdraws from them they are nothing any more, they no longer do anything good, and that is why they distrust themselves so much. I have noticed, you see, that those religious full of self-love, who want to appear more than they are, God humbles by making everything they do turn out badly.

Instead, look at the humble person: God seeks to exalt her… I could tell you so many instances that I would never finish, but I will only say that it is the truth of the Gospel that whoever humbles himself will be exalted and whoever exalts himself will be humbled.

My dear Franceschina,

Blessed be our Most Holy Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. I assure you, my daughter, that countless are the times I say: I must write to Franceschina, and so to my blessed daughters; but the crowd of occupations prevents me from doing what I so much desire and do so willingly. At this moment the Mother Delegate is packing the basket to send you; only I cannot put everything in, because we do not have it here in the house; so whatever you find missing, do not put it down to unwillingness to send it to you, but only to the fact that we are poor and do not have it. The sheets are fine ones: keep them in case someone comes to you. You will find two pieces of fine linen: they are for making pillowcases, and with them is the trimming, which you can detach and get them ready, because from what I have heard people from here may come to visit us. You will find two salamis: they are few, but we have hardly any left; I am sending you a prayer composed by the Superior, and he wishes the little girls to say it during their adoration throughout the novena, and the sisters too when they can; if it does not arrive in time for the novena, they can continue it all month. We have no more linen for chemises, unless Providence sends us some. Everything seems closed; let us leave it to the Lord, who works everything for the good of our souls. I am writing to Don Luigi. I am very sorry to find myself without time to do my duty; this letter I am writing I have taken up again for the fourth time. Since I arrived I have not yet received any letter from you. I fear for your health; take care of yourself. I am not well, but this morning I was able to give the meditation to our little girls. Let us remember, my daughters, that in these days we have the model of holy humility practiced by Jesus, and the Church keeps us occupied in these days teaching us how to imitate this model of every virtue, beginning with his going to the Jordan: to what abasement the Most Perfect, the most pure God-man was willing to submit, to be like a sinner, purified with the water of holy baptism in the Jordan; but heaven opened and a voice cried: This is my Son!

Jesus, what are you doing? But no! He goes on to subject his delicate humanity to greater torments. Let us look a little, my daughters: where are our mortifications of disordered sense, our abstinence from all that our Rules forbid us?

Ah, this is what our dear Jesus wants of our whole soul, for these are what will lead us to eternal life. Pray and love one another all with the same love, and take care to reach that beautiful unity of thought and action, so that all together you may form one heart and one mind, since you all tend towards one center, which is God; and so true charity and love among you must be so sincere that one's own good is also the good of one's sister. If you become like this, the spirit of God will reign in you for an eternity. God bless you and make you grow in perfection, so as to become his spouses.

I am your poor Mother Rosa

Piacenza, 9.3.70

My little daughter, I am sending you a form for rendering the accounts. I would like you to supervise the orphanage a little more. From certain reports I hear that the girls are somewhat neglected and that you do not agree among yourselves in giving penances. You must support one another; when you give a penance it must be upheld, and likewise when the others punish someone you must support them. If there is something that seems to you not right, you must warn them in private. So, for charity's sake, this is an important point. I do not want you to be alarmed by these remarks of mine; they must only help you to carry out each of your duties better. I commend Sr. A. I am sending you the form for the half-year.

Goodbye, your most affectionate Mother Rosa.

A Francesco Gattorno a Genoa, 24.8.1866, from Piacenza

Peace be with us. Dear good papa, because of certain gossip that echoes even as far as here in Piacenza, I have decided to tell you about it, having already had long talks with you on the subject. Now, my papa, you must allow me [to speak] with all confidence, just as if we were sitting in the piazza of San Luca having an academic discussion; so let us come to it, but without the slightest uneasiness, just talking: this time it is a sermon that does not end with the collection as usual; no, money does not come into it; it is only a question of making ourselves happy on both sides and of seeing how far offense to God can be avoided, God who protects you so much, so that one day we may live happily under his standard for eternity. From this opening you will already have understood: from hearing certain things continually repeated that do so little honor to our family, which, thanks to the goodness of a father and the exemplary conduct of the Mother, enjoyed the esteem and veneration of the whole city. Now what do you expect, dear father: this son of yours, Emanuele, whether it is passion or something else that keeps him bound to a woman whom, it seems, he loves, but who, out of love for his father and so as not to displease you in any way, will not make up his mind one way or the other. What will you say now? That [I am] mad and something more. My God, but meanwhile the scandal goes on, and still? What a life! Ah, for pity's sake, for the love that you, good Father, have had and still have for us, your most unworthy children, for we have all displeased you, I first of all; and yet you did not delay in doing me good, and now you have provided abundantly for me and my children, though I was married, so that when I think of it I cannot express the regret I feel at seeing how badly I have always repaid you; so, for the love and reverence we owe to the Divine Majesty of God, do not send me away unheard. Listen, dear father: if you will not give him your consent, at least close one eye and let him settle everything properly.

Considered well as regards her conduct, people of standing have assured me for a long time that her life is excellent and that she goes to Church a little; and then as regards money there would be nothing to say, for she is a woman with a reasonable dowry and still has the use of the income of her young children; he would be settled and would need nothing more, whereas living this way, what savings can be made? You understand well enough without my explaining further. I want to hope that you will not want this matter to go on any longer in this way, but that I shall certainly receive a couple of lines of consolation, seeing every offense to my good God removed.

If this letter displeases you, throw it in the fire, and as though nothing had happened we will stop talking of it and pray with resignation that the Lord may put forth his almighty arm and set everything right. Greet mamma and everyone for me.

Believe me wholly your daughter, Rosa Gattorno

Alla Principessa Emilia of Fitalia, from Rome

Dearest Daughter, last night I received yours with the photographs of Saint Anne enclosed. I am answering all your dear questions at once. First of all I thank you for the beautiful and dear expressions of affection in it, assuring you that they are most welcome to me; and the affection you show me I feel is most dear to me, and I assure you that I hold you close many times at the feet of my dear Crucified. I weep before my dear Madonna to obtain your grace, and I remind my holy Mother Saint Anne of her painful barrenness, and through the sufferings she endured at that time I beg her to see to appeasing God and giving you, my dear daughter, a child after the Heart of God. These are the prayers I make. But I am wretched and a poor sinner who can obtain nothing. Only the Blood of my dear Crucified can do everything with the heart of his eternal Father. Knock and do not grow weary, and it will be opened to you. As for my health, what shall I tell you? I was very ill, very high fevers left me very weak, but I am on my feet! Let us leave it to Jesus. (…) As for the photographs, what shall I tell you? Listen, I tell you what I feel, you will forgive me, won't you? I do not recognize Saint Anne at all; and the dear Child looks like a boy. What do you say? We have some very beautiful ones here in Rome, and if you tell me what you want to spend, I will commission someone to look for a beautiful one, and then I will see it. You must tell me the height and the price. I will make sure it is devout and beautiful. What can I say? I have it in my head that the Saint was a very beautiful Woman. What do you say? She was certainly a beautiful soul, to give birth to such a Creature: the Mother of God. Mary! Mary! Yours for all ages in my dear Crucified

Affectionately, M. Rosa Gattorno

Alla Principessa Emilia of Fitalia, from Rome 15.?.1886

AMF

I have received your most esteemed letter and am answering at once. I am glad to hear you are well again. Dear Emilia, if you could see how much I have to do! On Sunday we have the blessing of the House and of the little inner chapel. It will be performed by His Eminence Cardinal Parocchi — at 3 in the afternoon. I will hold you close to me. Carla had the baby girl, but I was not there; I arrived two hours after she was born. It was a misunderstanding, for she was to come and call me but did not understand properly. Oh, dear daughter! What is Mary Most Holy doing? You tell me she is cold. No, my dear, it is Jesus at work, and knowing he has good soil he works it with dryness of spirit, but hidden from your eyes he is close to you and guides all your actions. Courage, for much is gained in the time of trial. Saint Teresa was sad when she had all those delicacies, and why? She thought that tribulations would follow; but when she was in tribulation she was cheerful, because she awaited the joy that was to come. That is what you must do. Yes, the pain of love. To love and not to feel or see the Beloved is a most painful thing, but this hard trial is rewarded by dear, most sweet Jesus with certain caresses of his! Oh, my dear Emilia, be all Charity towards the poor, love much, give many alms. By them you will draw down all the blessings of heaven, and the dear Saviour will favor you in a special way. Forgive me if I dare to write to you so freely. But since I am a mother to you, I cannot do otherwise. You are so closely united with me in my dear Crucified that I desire nothing but to see you a saint. Goodbye. My respects to the Prince, and believe me

your affectionate M. Rosa

Alla Principessa Emilia of Fitalia, from Rome 18.8.1892

Dear daughter, I have been without letters from you for several days. Now I am writing to you with a request. Listen: there is a family that is literally dying of hunger, and so it would happen, for she was truly born a fine lady and now, abandoned by her husband with four children, they have nothing to eat. Listen, I know that charity alone obtains everything; well, I asked this unfortunate woman how much would be needed to provide a monthly allowance for bread and soup. She tells me that for the whole month it would be 45 lire, and I already have 20, and today I am to have more from another person; so one has given twenty, and I will hear from this other; but I should like you too to do this charity. She, poor mother, is a holy soul who prays a great deal, and I will have her pray for you, which she will certainly do in a special way. I await what [you give] each month: God will reward you. You see? Charity has no limits. I beg not only for the Lord's work, but also for those who are suffering.

Many respects to the Prince, and here they are working to prepare new things for your visit. Goodbye, receive a big embrace in my dear Crucified, and I am yours

Most affectionately, Mother Rosa

Alla Principessa Emilia of Fitalia, from Rome 5.3.1893

Dear daughter, I have received your letter, more than dear to me. I see your sadness with sorrow, but with a Mother's usual confidence I tell you that I see in it the hand of the enemy who troubles us. He already intends to harass you and is devising fine tricks. Above all he would like to put you in a bad temper, so as to make the Prince lose patience and so make you tiresome to him. So away with this; be strong, a true worker in the Lord's vineyard: cheerfully try to overcome every obstacle with peace and serenity; strong-minded as you are, you must fight and always win. It is half past three; the exposition of the Blessed Sacrament has just ended. I commended the matter of your lawsuit. Whatever court you go to, you will always lose it; it is useless to hope. As for selling your house, yes, it is in your interest to sell it. Sr. A. Teresa, coming like this, will have much to suffer from the devil, and on returning she will recover. Afterwards, however, she will come with me. The Heart of Jesus is pierced; what dreadful things will happen! Do not be afraid, not even for the Prince. The Novitiate will be very fine; those who dislike seeing the Daughters of Saint Anne grow, what will they say when they see a very great number coming from every part of Sicily… I am pleased that the work for the poor is going well. God bless it. Poor Sr. A. Teresa is very afraid of coming; poor thing, how dear she is, a treasure. Goodbye, ever yours in my dear Crucified, where I embrace you

Most affectionately, Mother Rosa

Alla Principessa Emilia of Fitalia, from Rome 29.5.1893

Dear daughter, what will you think, my dear Emilia, that after three letters from you I am only answering now! The work is great. My time passes in a quite extraordinary way. I assure you that in thought I am always with you, and I try in every way to share in what you are doing in God's work. Oh, good worker! How close the Most Holy Virgin and Saint Anne our Mother are to you! Oh, I would like you to be able to see them, and then you would be convinced that it is not an idea of mine, but that what I say is reality. I have read those two lines of your letter where you say that you are always thinking of the house and that you are making plans with the Cardinal; he was pleased, taking an interest in everything you do. So I would be of the opinion to put the two Sisters there, and the old man too, provided he is willing to go, because he will be afraid of losing his place. Enough, as regards the man I leave it entirely to you to make the best choice. As for the Sisters, others may go too to help (whenever there is need). I did not doubt that this would happen with Sr. A. Teresa as regards giving edification. Oh, if she did so much here, I can imagine how she behaves in that house. She is an angel, very pleasing to the Heart of Jesus… I will not speak to you of my health…

Dear Emilia, I have many sins to expiate; listen, I have good news for you: soon a house will be opened in Malta. Does it seem to you that the Holy Mother is on the move? Oh, dear Sr. A. Salvatore makes her sisters fly even outside Sicily… Be cheerful, for so many beautiful things are prepared for you.

Goodbye. Ever yours in my dear Crucified, and so in him a strong embrace, and my respects to the Prince and a kiss to Sr. A. Teresa.

Your most affectionate Mother Rosa

My beloved daughter, how pleased I was by your dear letter with such fine news! May God be thanked for it. Dear Emilia, how good you are; you attribute to me what does not belong to me, because what Jesus does he does for his Work, not because of the prayers of this ugly, wretched creature; I assure you I have nothing to do with your work, at which you labor and toil so hard so that everything may go well for the glory of God and of the Holy Mother. Alla Principessa Emilia of Fitalia, from Rome 12.2.1898

Beloved daughter, but what a terrible woman! After this account of so beautiful a death, you weep?!! What a fine grace: he did not even notice he was dying. Oh, blessed soul, to have had such a privilege! Confession, communion, and then he fell asleep in the Lord! Everything so well arranged that that unhappy woman did not deserve to hear him any more or have time to upset him! What a grace! Emilia, you weep! It is true you have lost him, but you will possess him for an eternity. That business of the will was a fine thing; certainly having remade it was a great good, for he would not have been so serene and peaceful, and those poor unfortunate boys, where would that money have ended up? A great privilege! The children will know their mother when they are older; now they cannot understand it, and one day they will bless their Father for having provided for them so well. Nothing surprises me, because how much she made poor Alessandro suffer! It is beyond belief that such barbarity should reign in a heart, but they are to be pitied and forgiven, because I am convinced they do not understand the harm they do. They feel little, they live only for greed of money and comfort; they think everyone must think that way. Poor creatures, their life is unhappy, because they never have peace. Yes, forgive her as you have already done, and calm your poor heart by tormenting it less, thinking of the great graces the good brother had from Jesus, so much comfort and strength, without suffering the atrocious pangs of death; but he fell asleep peacefully! Who would not envy him?

[I] am getting better and better and preparing for the journey. I shall stop two days in Naples, and you will be told beforehand.

Many respects to the Prince. To you a big embrace in my dear Crucified.

Most affectionately, M. Rosa

Prayer of Father Tornatore

«Eternal Divine Father, we give you thanks that, having made use of our glorious Mother Saint Anne and Father Saint Joachim to give the world the mother of its Saviour, you have bound all creatures to particular sentiments of love and gratitude towards them. But on the other hand, seeing that the world did not pay this debt of esteem, praise and gratitude to its Benefactors, you were pleased to raise up our poor Institute in your Church to stand surety for this debt. Ah, grant that we may be faithful to this most noble vocation, ever occupied in honoring the venerable Woman, the Mother of Mary Immaculate, the grandmother of our Saviour. We honor her by acknowledging her as our Mother, which is to say as your minister in sanctifying us, giving us through her prayers the life of grace, the divine life which, making us sharers in your own nature, makes us your adopted daughters, your spouses and heirs of your glory. We honor her by filling ourselves with her spirit of faith, hope and charity, imitating her in her virtues of simplicity, prudence, humility and meekness; imitating her in her virtues of poverty, chastity, modesty, detachment from relatives and obedience; in her virtues of devotion to poor girls in danger, compassion for the sick, charity towards our neighbor and towards our enemies. We honor her by sisterly love among ourselves, by filial love and respect for our superiors; by religion towards you, towards Jesus Christ in the adoration of the sacrament of his love, towards Mary Immaculate and towards her herself. And in this way, having built up her glory in the Church militant, may we be worthy to be her crown in the Church triumphant. Amen.»

Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, 4.2.1871

… let us bless the Lord for it, our help, our master, who knows so well how to teach us, and let us try to profit from his lessons and be diligent pupils so as to please him and fully satisfy his will; my Daughter, if you knew what consolation I feel just in uttering this phrase (pleasing God) and in being, or being able to become, his delight, I feel quite beside myself, so that if I had to face the cruelest martyrdom I would feel nothing; who could doubt it? Could there be any creature who thinks differently and does not feel what I say? No, I do not believe it; but if I knew there was someone who felt it more than I, I would weep, and with so much effort I would want to work to get ahead of her; ah, my Eternal Father! Daughter, the heart of this God is so beautiful and so loving that there are no words to express it.

Daughter, you know that charity blazes in this immense heart — it is its queen; so whoever does not have it cannot say that she shares in this his blazing love; how sweet it is to us when we can awaken a wholly pure affection for those creatures, however repulsive, and if our very blood were needed, we would quickly draw it from our veins to feed the poor man or the sick. Look at our good Father (Tornatore), see in him the portrait of charity: what delight can be read in his eyes when he provides for the sick and the poor, and how little he loves himself, and still more when with such zeal he tries to meet your needs, especially when you are ill, sparing nothing; I know too how much the means he provides for you cost him, but he cares nothing for it, nothing, he thinks only of relieving your sufferings with that little satisfaction for your human nature, which, still little schooled in virtue, feeds itself and sweetens its sufferings with material care for our most wretched body. I would like to add many other things, because when I speak of Charity, my daughter, it seems to me I would never stop; I find everything in it, every consolation, everything in a word; but I must stop because I have to attend to other very urgent matters; so we must always give up every pleasure of our own to serve God…

Prayer to the Eternal Father by Fr. G. B. Tornatore

«Eternal Divine Father, we firmly believe that you are the Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, who after his death descended into hell to triumph over the devil in the very heart… of his kingdom, to bring out from there the souls of the holy Fathers, who, having died with the gift of faith, hope and charity, were just, holy and his friends. Through this faith of ours, grant us the grace, for love of you, to care with great charity for every kind of poor sick person, to go down into their hovels, to share in all their ills, to bring relief to all their miseries, imitating in this way the compassion of our mother Saint Anne, mother of the Immaculate.

(XVI) «Eternal Divine Father, we firmly believe that you are the Father of our Lord Jesus, who in the resurrection will give the bodies of the elect their endowments: clarity, by which they will be more resplendent than the sun; impassibility, by which all tears will be wiped away and all sufferings removed, and they will overflow with pleasure and joy; agility, by which they will be in an instant wherever the spirit wishes; subtlety, by which, spiritualized, they will no longer be any burden to the spirit.

Through this faith of ours, grant that, imitating the charity of our glorious mother Saint Anne, mother of the Immaculate, we may generously overcome all the repugnance of the flesh in caring for the sick infected with any disease.

(XXIV)

Circular letter — Fr. Tornatore and M. Rosa, 1886

An Institute is in the flower of observance when the Spirit of Jesus Christ reigns in it. The Spirit of Jesus Christ shows itself chiefly in the charity that drove him to die for us. Now, by the mercy of God, the Institute showed itself full of this Spirit this year too.

The Lord afflicted the poor city of Palermo with cholera. While people, terrified by the dreadful pestilence, fled here and there, and the poor stricken by the disease were left abandoned, our sisters, filled with the charity of Jesus Christ, went into the midst of the slaughter; night and day they brought every kind of comfort, and they did not leave the victims until they were healed, or until they had placed the spirit of the dying in God's hands and their bodies in the grave. This spirit of evangelical courage, which cheerfully faced the dangers of death to save the lives of their brothers and sisters, filled with amazement not only the good but also the enemies of our holy religion; and in this way they caused Jesus Christ, the source of such charity, to be glorified by good and wicked alike.
