Circular letter Fr. Tornatore and Mother Rosa, 1.1.1880

… Negotiations are under way to found three more Houses, likewise there in America, in three different cities, for which 40 Sisters would be called. This eagerness to have our sisters arises from seeing the fine results obtained by the people who have them, both in hospitals and in schools. One of these blessings that the Lord is pleased to bestow on his creatures through the hands of our sisters, and which deserves special mention, is the distribution of soup to the poor. In this winter of seventy-nine and eighty the Lord is punishing the sins of the world with cold and hunger. Well, his mercy, which is never separated from his divine justice, has called us, his ministers, to help so many wretched people, distributing food and clothing to them every day. In the Mother House alone about three thousand beggars are fed with good, well-seasoned soup. What a great grace this is, O Sisters! What a sign of predilection the Lord gives us! The way to thank him for such a distinction is to humble ourselves before his divine Majesty, sincerely acknowledging ourselves unworthy, and to work without sparing ourselves to carry out so noble a task. The number of those who received the habit was 57, a lower number than that of '78; but the cause was not a shortage of postulants… but that, owing to the critical times we are living in, they were not able to bring the dowry that is required, little as it is. On the other hand, the Mother House, given the hardship of the times, has not been able to open its arms to receive them without a dowry. And here comes the point to be especially recommended to Superiors: economy, so that after maintaining and clothing the sisters they may send the surplus to the mother house. To this they are bound by love, by vow and by justice. By love, they must know that the fruitfulness of the Institute depends on two points: the first is that the Lord should call many, even with a very small dowry or none at all. Now the first point was not lacking this year, for the requests were very many; but the Mother House lacked the means to receive them without a dowry. And on whom does it depend that the Mother House should have these means? It depends precisely on the economy practiced by the Superiors.

It is consoling to say that many true daughters of the Holy Mother, eager to see her family spread throughout the world, are most careful to account for every last cent, as the saying goes, so as to have a surplus to send to the Mother House, knowing that on its well-being depends the well-being of the whole Institute. The Mother House is the heart of the Institute. If the heart is full of life, the limbs of the other Houses too are healthy and strong. But the Holy Mother does not receive this joy from all. There are some spendthrifts who, in spite of handsome allowances, never have anything to save. These are without love and without natural feeling, who care nothing for the glory of the Institute. Besides lacking love for the Institute, these put themselves in danger of failing in justice by harming it… let them remember that they are not owners of the property of the Houses over which they preside but mere administrators. And it is worth noting that, just as Superiors who love the Institute and take care not to squander its goods also treat their sisters well, love them when healthy and care for them when sick, so those who live only for themselves and cannot save neglect the sisters and make them suffer…

Circular letter — Fr. Tornatore and Mother Rosa, 1887

… Filial love for the Holy Mother is the source of all the graces of heaven. The Holy Mother is the one who leads those who are her true daughters to devotion to Mary Most Holy Immaculate, her daughter; she leads them to the practice of all the virtues proper to their vocation; she leads them to the love of God, in which love holiness consists. Many of these good daughters of the Saint have shown outstanding spirit of sacrifice this year too: they courageously undertook very long journeys, they went to America, to Bolivia, to Brazil; they went to Africa, heedless of the many dangers met with on such long and arduous journeys.

This spirit of sacrifice was shown by those assigned to the care of the sick stricken by contagious diseases, stricken by black smallpox, stricken by the terrible scourge of cholera. These sisters behaved with such charity and such generosity that they were a spectacle to heaven and earth. They faced death with such joy that they seemed already to see paradise opened, the reward of their charity.

These blessings that the Holy Mother pours out on her Institute must spur all of us ever more to long for her with an ever more tender and ardent love, as these good daughters have shown in all their steps; yes, we repeat that this love for their Mother leads to the holiness God requires of them.

Alongside these virtues, however, we point out a fault, so that once known it may be corrected by those who recognize it in themselves. This fault concerns, in the first place, poverty. There are Superiors who are negligent in sending the half-yearly account on time, and with it the surplus. This fault is certainly not slight, for it throws into disorder the ledger in which these must be entered, and harms the Institute, because without the surplus… we cannot carry out the transactions planned for the Institute's benefit.

Aspects of our poverty as Daughters of Saint Anne in the thought of the Founders

It grieves me to hear you are always under the press of the bitterest tribulations — and now we have the impossible proposal of the House that they want the Daughters of Saint Anne to take on! Oh, certainly, if they had credits and millions it would be fine! But long live poverty! — Where is the money to come from? Oh, is this all the good and interest they have for us? Oh, how flattering the world is, and how little, not to say nothing, it amounts to — certain proposals make me laugh — who has taken on the newspaper? Certainly it is not the Belmontes, I assure you; but it is time to open our eyes and watch our step — as for the houses, I will think about it, but the expense they have incurred seems too much — they must remember that we live on providence and not get it into their heads to do more than can be done — isn't that so? I am thinking how best to arrange everything — patience and time — I would like to see our business and then!…

SOURCE: LETTER by M. Rosa to Cardinal G. di Belmonte — 25.11.1892 · Archive ref.: MIB A.2.18

At this moment I am in Genoa and am taking this minute to write to you, so that you may have time to do what I would like to find ready. Not only the guest quarters in order and clean, but the whole house as well, especially the kitchen… let us hope the Lord will send us everything: all to him, all — and to us confusion and humiliation, annihilation, shame. I am truly nothing but a wretched servant of the Lord — let me write to you so (real dung).

You write to me about money — I have a little, but it is certainly not enough. Dear God will send the rest — did Saint Joseph not bring some?

On Wednesday the 29th at half past eleven we shall be at the station… Please be kind to whoever you find with me, so that she is not left alone or received ungraciously.

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni — 25.3.1871 · Archive ref.: MIF 1871 A.2.14

… as for money, spend it as the Father tells you (…) Now, my daughter, for charity's sake, do not let yourself be taken by whims and vague ideas, things that confuse the mind and serve only to disturb us and make us irritable. Let us keep to what is positive and take great care always to reason with the Crucifix before us, not at our side; let us look at him in all our actions, to see whether they conform to his model, and then everything comes to nothing, and our sufferings become a mere nothing, less than nothing.

Our daughter, where are your cruel sufferings? I cannot find them, for while I look at my Jesus and then at his Spouse, Sr. A. Maria Adelaide, I see nothing that could be set against the least of his wounds. I look for her suffering and do not find even enough to relieve the least pain of Jesus. Do your teeth ache? Well, Jesus had them all smashed and his mouth was streaming with blood; do you find no one to tell your troubles and afflictions to? I see a Father who comforts you and this poor Mother of yours, who would give anything to make you a true crucified one, so that one day you may die on the bed of Jesus and then [go] to Paradise for an Eternity; there is no more cross there, there are no more sufferings — only love, love… Be cheerful, for Jesus loves those who suffer: whoever does not want to suffer does not want to love.

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni — 16.7.1870 [?] · Archive ref.: MIF 1870 A.2.14

And you, poor thing, how do you manage? But I assure you I am always thinking of it…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa — recipient unknown — 29.4.1877 · Archive ref.: MIF 77 A.2.14

My dear, I am writing to you seated on a loom bench, almost on the floor, with the noise of the looms deafening me.

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 7.7.1869 · Archive ref.: MIF 1869 A.2.14

… Listen, now that Don A… is no longer there, I would like you to tell Sr. A. Santina (as if it came from you) to put aside the money she receives and then send it to me, of course a month's worth, after deducting expenses, and that she should pay for the flour herself. In this way she would get used to managing by herself; what do you think? Listen, I am suggesting this to you, but do it only if you think it right — think it over and then do what you have decided… Urge her to see that the Sisters are well fed, that the bread is good; this is my wish; since Providence is coming in, let them see that nothing is lacking — no waste, nothing against the dear jewel of poverty, but not too little and poor food either, since they have much hard work…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 1874 · Archive ref.: MIF 1874 A.2.14

… at this moment the Mother Delegate is packing the basket to send you; only I cannot put everything in, because we do not have it here in the house; so whatever you find missing, do not put it down to unwillingness to send it to you, but only to the fact that we are poor and do not have it. The sheets are fine ones: keep them in case someone comes to you. You will find two pieces of fine linen: they are for making pillowcases, and with them is the trimming, which you can detach and get them ready, because from what I have heard people from here may come to visit you. You will find two salamis — they are few, but we have hardly any left… We have no more linen for chemises, unless providence sends us some. Everything seems closed; let us leave it to the Lord, who works everything for the good of our souls.

(…) Let us remember, my Daughters, that in these days we have the model of holy humility practiced by Jesus, and the way to imitate this example of every virtue, beginning with his going to the Jordan, that abasement… Let us look a little, my daughters: where are our mortifications of disordered sense, our abstinence from all that our rules forbid us?

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 9.3.1870 · Archive ref.: MIF 1870 A.2.14

… Blessed be Jesus, who has put so much generosity into the heart of that benefactress! You tell me she weighed the linen and cloth, which are not ours, that is, that the linen brought there is theirs, but hers if she has locked it away — here, little daughter, I see nothing harsh, for it is well known that linen is a very delicate matter; it means that your Religious will provide themselves with it little by little. I also hear of the archpriest's eagerness soon to set up the chapel there, where they will reserve the Blessed Sacrament — oh, Paradise! How happy are the daughters of Saint Anne who have the privilege of having Jesus in their family!

You ask me whether it is prudent to ask Maddalena for the allowance of 350 francs. After so much generosity on her part, I do not think it prudent to ask for it, but leave it to her to give it when she thinks fit.

I am quite certain that if you asked for it we would commit a lack of trust towards Maddalena, who so generously prepared the most necessary provisions.

Now to the hospital: I tell you that if Sr. Anna Tomasina cannot keep the Religious on one franc a day, either she is a spendthrift or she makes the sisters live in too much luxury and not according to the poverty of the Institute.

First, point out to her that at Ovada there are six sisters, and yet four have one franc a day, actually less, that is 300 francs, and two only 200 francs, and yet they live without debts; at Nice they certainly do not have more than one franc a day and they manage — indeed Sr. Anna Giuseppa has even saved something, which she gave to the Mother.

Secondly, let us work out the day's expenses: I suppose each eats a pound and a half of bread a day — amazing! We here at San Lazzaro have young men of 20-25, and yet they have three 5-ounce loaves a day: one at breakfast, one at dinner and one at supper; so now that bread was at 60 centimes a kilo, the cost of bread for each sister per day would be 30 centimes; allow another 30 centimes a head for the main dish, and that is ample; I allow 20 centimes a head for soup; then I allow for seasoning and for coffee and sugar… so you see they can live comfortably on one franc a day and buy the little things needed for sewing and washing; and the wine, as the rule requires, must be well watered, and it would not be well watered unless it were half water.

I suppose, for example, that if pieces of bread are left over at breakfast, they do not waste them but use them to make bread soup. I imagine that at least twice a week they will make bread soup, and at least once polenta cooked in broth, also as the soup at the day's table: we eat it here in the College, and will the poor daughters of Saint Anne not eat it?

I suppose they mix a little chicory with the coffee; I suppose the two main dishes a day are not all meat, but especially the second with just a little meat; they will add a side dish of beans or potatoes or greens.

I suppose they are not too fond of spices. In short, the Holy Mother wants them to have enough to live on to serve the Lord, but not to indulge greed and comfort.

Here Poss has sent a letter to the Mother, or to whoever acts for her, setting out the whole allowance he intends to give for the girls: keep it, and then he will write to the Mother. My greetings to Maddalena… and to the sisters; as for Maddalena, God willing I will soon pay her a visit. As for Poss's letter, I would like you not to send it to the Mother until we have talked it over together. Jesus yours forever…

SOURCE: LETTER by Fr. Tornatore — recipient unknown — 20.3.1874 [?] · Archive ref.: TaL 74-14 A.1.1

«Eternal Divine Father, we firmly believe that you are the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who became incarnate by the Holy Spirit, was born of the Virgin Mary and became man. Through this faith of ours, grant us the grace to be detached from the goods of this earth, so that we have nothing with us but what is given or permitted to us by our Superiors. Let us take nothing of the things held in common, nothing of things left lying about. Let us give, lend or exchange nothing; keep nothing locked away, carry nothing from one house to another, accept nothing as a gift, loan or exchange without our Superior's permission. Let us show nothing, in words or in deeds, that suggests the least attachment to things; so that we may be perfect copies of the poverty of our glorious mother Saint Anne, mother of Mary Immaculate.

SOURCE: PRAYERS ALL’ETERNO PADRE composte dal P.G.B. Tornatore · Archive ref.: laP 1 (XI) A.1.0

A few moments ago I received a letter of yours dated the 22nd of this month. I am glad to hear that God sent you a little providence; let us thank this dear treasurer of ours.

I would like to know, when you write to me, whether you have paid the pharmacist and how much is still owed to the miller, and the other accounts. Let us pray that the Lord may send us his providence, and let us never lose courage — always trusting in God's mercy, never distrusting.

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni n. 7 · Archive ref.: MIF x-11 A.2.15

… you cannot imagine how sorry I am to hear that providence is not favoring you there either. My dear, listen, one really has to say that it is truly my sins that make us groan so; here everyone owes us and we cannot get [payment] for our work from anyone, others promise us and nothing ever comes; would you believe it, I have not a cent. Patience; what humiliations, my dear! This time the Holy Mother really wants to bend our pride with the greatest humiliations; so be it. As soon as I have anything, half will be yours.

… Dear Francesca, if the days in this vale of misery are bitter, just as sweet and consoling will be the Eternity you will have always with Jesus. SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 1.10.1869 · Archive ref.: MIF 1869 A.2.14

… I hear from the Delegate [of the Casa] del Verme that she will give you a little money — you see that Providence never fails. And with God's help we must try to put it into practice. Who was poorer than Jesus? And if we are to be his imitators, we must always be in the stables…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni — 18.6.1871 · Archive ref.: MIF 1871 A.2.14

Just two lines, because it is very late. All is going well; I hope providence will come to that house too, for when the work is wholly God's it certainly cannot fail. I know nothing about the one at Pontedecimo; she had promised so much, but it is quite true that the Saint wants us to practice poverty, and if I did otherwise, I assure you, they would become an abyss of pride worse than Lucifer. SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — undated · Archive ref.: MIF.C.x. 17

… My God, do with us what you will, isn't that so, my dear Franceschina? I am answering your letter; I feel your afflictions more than ever and I am hastening at once to find a way to relieve you of at least part of them.

… Dear Francesca, without my telling you how poor we are, you know it… I am truly pierced by the lance on every side, but always on the cross crying: long live Jesus, may his holy will be done in us. Patience in the midst of so many sufferings…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 2.7.1869 · Archive ref.: MIF 1869 A.2.14

I have received your letters, and particularly the last one telling me about the mattress… I would have liked to have news of the nursing of the sick. Let us hope that good Jesus will deign to let himself be cared for by the poor daughters of his great Grandmother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. Daughter, courage and patience; you will see that soon the Lord will come with special providence; I am very sorry about it, and my anxiety is such that my breast is as if between two stones, but I lack nothing of trust in God the Father — he will provide when we least expect it. Let us pray fervently, so that our prayers may reach the loving heart of Jesus, where the source of all spiritual and temporal riches is found. See to the observance of the Holy Rules, another most powerful means of having the right hand of the Eternal Father favorable to us — dear hand which, wherever it points its gentle finger, heals all our wounds. Daughter, love this dear Eternal Father and make your daughters love him, for if they love this God the Father, our one and only good, they will become perfect and be able to do whatever they like, for everything will be well done… Daughters, stand firm and put all your trust in God. Clasp and love your privations, the discomfort your poor human nature must endure — keep these treasures carefully and offer them joyfully to your dear Eternal Father, that he may deign to accept and keep them, changing them into some little treasure of his… May God grant that you may taste this honey of suffering, which is the essence of all good…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti — 22.5.1871 [?] · Archive ref.: MIF 1871 A.2.14

… my little daughter, this is already the fifth day I have been in this Holy City and I have done nothing yet, obtained nothing yet. Let us pray, yes, do it fervently; let us pray the Heart of Jesus to move the hearts of good people to help the work of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. He alone can, because he must exert himself in this work of his Grandmother, since it belongs to his Eternal Father. My Jesus, what work should be dearer to your heart than this? Unless it be that in which your Father is glorified! These poor creatures, daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, have him continually on their lips, invoke him in all their actions, keep him in their hearts, because they love him as Father, placing all their good in him; they adore him in his most exalted Dignity, in his Divinity… in short, you can say: they are the true daughters of my Eternal Father, because they expect everything from him and rest in him alone — my Jesus, is this not true? And can your heart delay in coming to the help of these creatures in what they need, and especially of the one most in need of all, your slave… My God! The moment in which I find myself is so important. What a great concern fills my mind. Patience! May God be blessed in all things…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 1.6.1871 · Archive ref.: MIF 1871 A.2.14

So Saint Anne wants a fine House — to work quickly, and then I will come to the fine ceremony of the first stone. Oh, how fearful you are, always afraid that the Lord's Providence will not come — it is a bottomless sack; whoever trusts in him alone knows that he has everything — it is absolutely certain; it must be done at once…

SOURCE: LETTER by M. Rosa to Cardinal G. di Belmonte — 8.11.1890 [?] · Archive ref.: MIB A.2.18

… A few days ago I was very distressed because I lacked the money to pay a bill they wanted settled at once. My God! What providence: after praying hard, a few hours after I finished my prayer a lady came and brought me all I needed, telling me she had been sent by someone to bring me that money; and though I did all I could to find out who had sent her, she would tell me nothing, repeating: this unknown person; pray; and she left me! I was overwhelmed and rushed to the chapel to thank my God of providence, who deigned to send it to me…

… I lacked the means to feed so many sisters and girls, and I could not go out begging because my liver was very painful… and I had a fever. What was I to do? I began to weep at the feet of my Crucified: what can I do? Why do you not provide for your creatures? I am ill. Are you displeased with what I do, does it not please you? While I was praying like this, behold a good supply of goods arriving from far away. Oh, my Love! When shall I be yours for an Eternity? “It is true, you will have all you need” — his words.

p. 102

… I made a novena to the Most Holy Trinity to send me providence, as I was in need; and behold, in rapture I was shown a person holding a little bag of gold in his hand and bringing it to me (it was true). He came at once; I was so convinced that my Good would see to providence that I no longer pray for it…

SOURCE: Madre Rosa Gattorno — MEMOIRS · Archive ref.: Mmm-1 Parte I A.3.32

… My daughters, you well know how dear poverty is to this Mother of yours. She loves it, embraces it and always clasps it to her breast. But my soul is wounded by you on this account, because I see that you love it little and, to put it better, do not know it. Listen, I cannot find words to make you know its exquisiteness; I will only tell you that it is the treasure of the saints. Yes, we are poor and we rejoice in it. They will have nothing to do with it — My God, what sorrow! — and so the Holy Mother forces you to embrace it, and in your House providence is much less than in all the others — do you understand?

… make her a novena to send you, that is, to obtain for you from God the Father, Providence, and with it the gift of practicing poverty and loving it; that she may obtain for you a taste for this treasure; and meanwhile promise God that with his Divine Help you will practice it…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni — 4.9.1872 · Archive ref.: MIF 1872 A.2.14

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Gaudenzia Martinelli — 30.11.1883 · Archive ref.: MIF 1883 A.2.15

… Since the promise I made you to keep you with me in spirit, and so to bring you to the feet of my Crucified every morning, makes you feel something of what happens to me, this is that spiritual union obtained by means of prayer; without it nothing can be had. Hold it for certain that prayer is the key to graces: it opens the Lord's treasury and draws from it as it pleases.

… Trust, my daughter; truly your mother assures you that the greater the degree of trust one has in God, the more provident his mercy becomes towards us, pouring out providence on every side. Courage! You ask me for the habits: yes, they will be ready at once and I will send them to you.

You will tell Papa that I will send him the cloth too, because I think it will be to his taste; as for the price, I want him to set it… What, my papa asks me the price of the goods? Never. He must do everything as he has always done everything for me, so exactly… How gladly I would send you money, but if you saw what an effort I am making, how much is needed here, you would certainly get a fever just like me…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 18.9.1869 · Archive ref.: MIF 1869 A.2.14

SOURCE: Madre Rosa Gattorno — MEMOIRS · Archive ref.: Mmm-7 A.3.32

… as the day of the great ineffable mystery of love draws near, which gives us everything to feel and taste and to learn to love and to feed on this most living love…

King of heaven and earth, nothing but a handful of straw and a few linens to wrap you in

pp. 42-43

SOURCE: Madre Rosa Gattorno — MEMOIRS · Archive ref.: Mmm-7 A.3.32

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni — 8.11.1872 [?] · Archive ref.: MIF 1872 A.2.14

… you promised me you would pray and be present at the Community prayers — Yes, my dear, prayers are the adornment of our actions; what if we offer our God an imperfect piece of work? Ah, bliss beyond compare: we, God's delight! Ah, my little daughter, what joy! There is nothing on this earth like it. You have so often told me, and shown me by deeds, your love for me, for which I am extremely grateful, but how happy I would be if you confirmed it by giving me proof that you love God very much and feel a great love for him — I assure you this happiness would greatly relieve my burdens. Come, then, come with me to Calvary for love of our Crucified, to be his alone and with him on the cross…

SOURCE: LETTER by Mother Rosa to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa — 15.10.1874 · Archive ref.: MIF 1874 A.2.14

… listen, my daughter: in your letter you tell me you are not well; well then, for charity's sake, take care of yourself and give me exact reports, for that is my wish… I also see that you are in low spirits, you are distressed, and why, my Franceschina? Courage! You want to follow your poor Mother and do not know what road hers is. … Let us take poverty and see to what sublimity it is raised: we have nothing, everything can be taken from us, and blessed will be the Daughter of Saint Anne who can put it into practice…

Or should they not all be equal?… We have found ourselves, it is true, without anything, but at the moment of paying the bills the money comes. And is this not all the providence of the Lord?

The Lord wants us to observe poverty in poverty itself, so that afterwards, in greatness, we may know how to put it into practice. The person who knows how to practice it when means are scarce will know how to practice it in prosperity too. Whereas those who in scarcity let everything go to waste and take no account of anything, partly from diabolical suggestion, partly from their bad habits, how much will they waste in abundance? We are bound to put this vow scrupulously into practice to acquire the virtue; and Jesus himself… born… in a stable, in the utmost poverty, willed to observe this virtue all the more…

SOURCE: CONFERENCE VIII — Madre Rosa — 25.2.1871 — Sampierdarena · Archive ref.: MmC 1.1 A.3.36

Today I will insist on the point of Poverty, because this point can never be explained and put into practice enough. You know, O Sisters, that to go to Paradise one must be poor. This vow goes against our human nature, but it pleases Our Lord so much that he chose it as his inheritance: he willed to be born poor, of a poor Virgin, in a stable where there was nothing but a little straw. We are poor, but let us see how far we are from the [poverty] of the stable of Bethlehem. Let us see how much we neglect this Vow. (…) We have left the world and consequently everything; and what is the use of wearing ourselves out at the bedsides of the sick, and of the teachers exhausting their lungs over the girls, if then for some worthless rag spoiled we must lose the crown prepared for us? You will say to me: “Mother can speak to us of nothing else; we are poor enough.” Oh, my sisters, a Saint Teresa insisted on this point, and her [nuns] were poorer than we (…) Thank God we lack nothing; in church we have chairs to sit on, and what more do we want? The vow of Poverty detaches us from everything, but it does not dispense us from keeping things in order (…)

Come now, I hope you will put this Vow into practice; especially to those who fail in it I leave it as their examen for the whole month; likewise to those who fail in silence I leave silence; to those who fail in obedience I leave obedience.

Now I want to remove a fear that has arisen in some of you, namely that as soon as you fall ill you will be sent away. Ah no! You have had proofs that the sick are kept and cared for with diligence and charity; you see, the sick are dearer to me, because, as we know, they have been visited by the Lord with an illness; it is for quite other reasons that sisters are sent away…

SOURCE: CONFERENCE XXI — Madre Rosa — 25.5.? — Piacenza · Archive ref.: MmC 1.1 A.3.36

If poverty was embraced by Our Lord Jesus Christ as the greatest treasure, which he loved so much, how much we must try to practice it! Let us look at Our Lord, the Father of heaven and earth, brought low, humiliated (…) Going to Calvary we see him thirsty, deprived of a drop of water; on the cross he had no one to support his head crowned with thorns. Oh, Poverty, if a God who could have had all kingdoms sought you, then there is something delightful in you that no one knows.

My God, King of heaven and earth, all kingdoms, all royal mantles rich with gold are yours, and yet I see you without a tunic to cover yourself. So I will always repeat: poverty, how great you are! You will say to me: you call a thing that is nothing great? Yes: if God chose it, how much must a Religious love it whom God has placed to practice it in his House, she who lives in the dwelling of the Lord! How fortunate we shall be if we try to put it into practice, to love it, to drink it in, in the dwelling of the Lord. He has placed poverty in his House as Queen, attaching a vow to it. The founders made it the foundation of their foundations.

And what does vow mean? It is to bind oneself, to cling to something. The vow says to you: I bind you to this, and while you are patched, those patches will be so many stars shining in heaven. See: I, poor in a tomb, wrapped in a shroud, but then you see me in heaven glorious and triumphant — all paradise, all the blessed hosts humbling themselves before me.

All around him enjoy his beatitude. And what does he do? He inebriates them all and fills them with paradise by his presence, by his love.

Yes, let us call poverty Queen, for whoever has the good fortune to embrace it here on earth is the one on whose head it will set the crown of glory in paradise; whoever has embraced it closely will come nearer to Our Lord. If a Religious does not bother to patch her habit because she thinks the Superior will then make her a new one, she fails in poverty; she does not bother to patch it or clean it, saying: this way it changes color and the Superior is obliged to make me a new one — oh God, how this Religious fails in poverty! And so one sees that great body of hers dressed in new clothes. 1st we must use every care to make our habit last; 2nd we must see that nothing is spoiled (…) you are in the House of Saint Anne, and what did you come into Religion for, if not to enjoy delights?

So let us profit from this fine treasure, so holy that no words can be found to express how great this treasure is. The Church teaches it to me, and Jesus Christ himself with his person — he does not want to teach us by word but by his own example, so that we too may set our feet where he set his. Our Houses are indeed poor, but do you know why we do not yet know how to love and practice this virtue? If we go, for example, to a rich monastery, you will see how quickly we adapt; but where there is Poverty, can you tell me how hard it is to adapt? Oh, how much this body, which longs for softness, has to suffer! Someone will think she has attained [it] because perhaps she has a hard straw mattress or an old mattress or the like. No, do not believe it, for the saints themselves had to suffer from it.

(…) Let us try, then, to imitate the saints in poverty, humility, chastity and obedience, who obeyed the lowliest on this earth; let us not think we are something, but rather the last of all.

To the girls of Piacenza, 4.2.1871

Enter, O my little daughter, into yourself and answer me. My soul is making its way to eternal life, to my homeland; and it is a very moving answer, for if I am not made of stone, faith awakens and says to me: to your center, for I was sent by God himself to sustain your body. I am a pure spirit created in the image of God, and I must return to him as beautiful as he created me. I, poor thing, who live in the prison of this body, so ill-treated, so despised, hear it say to me: by its straying you have made me die so many times. But a day will come when you will be separated for an eternity. Daughters, think: if a portion of yourselves were taken from your breast, would that portion not long to return to where all delights are for an eternity? O my soul, you are right to cry out: a wretched pleasure granted to our body will separate us from our God for an eternity. Daughters, the words of the Church are words of the Holy Spirit, of God himself; do we believe these two truths? Do we believe in the Passion of the Lord, in the point we read this morning? Do we perhaps think it is all lies, or that someone who believes in the Church comes to teach us untrue things? Daughters, the words of the Saints are words spoken by that most pure and holy mouth of Jesus, who had nothing doubtful to say to man; could the Redeemer allow his words to be contradicted, or even to be doubtful? Daughters, let us remember that the Word of God is as precious as the pupil of our eye: once it is lost one sees nothing any more, the way that leads us to Paradise is lost, and once this way is lost we find ourselves in the mud, in the midst of the sorrow of this world. Daughters, think seriously: everything you are told and God teaches you, I can assure you, is all words of truth of Holy Church; I take them from that holy truth of the Gospel, and I want nothing but that they be impressed on your minds so that you may become good Christians. Ah, my daughters, how hard the conduct of some of you is for me! What sorrow it causes me! And how many prayers I have said to ask the Lord for the grace that you may enter into yourselves and profit from these days of mercy the Lord grants you, and from what the Confessor and the teachers come to instill in you. I beg the Most High to open your hearts, so that they may not remain closed by those passions that so defile your souls. Oh, how many graces our Jesus has given you! How many there are who would like to come in; how many, when I go out, I see in the streets, dirty, ragged, without clothes, who look at me with a look of compassion. They lie on the ground, which serves them as a bed, and live like animals, having nothing Christian about them but their soul. These poor girls have no guide to comfort them in their troubles, no mothers to care for them. How many graces, then, he has given you! I repeat to you what I have told you so many times: the world leads to perdition. I do not tell you to become religious, but only that your actions should surpass all creatures in the fragrance of holiness and in virtue.

Do you perhaps think that in speaking to you like this I want you to be religious, to be saints, spouses of Jesus? Ah no, I want you to become those Christian mothers who are the blessing of the families they enter, who so often by their good example lead a straying soul back to the right path, inviting it to the feet of the priest, to reflect on the wounds of its soul, its failings, and finally to come away purified and consoled.

Daughters, listen: how long it is since I came back to make you know the beauty of this sacrament, how great it is and how well disposed we must be to receive the fruits it brings. Daughters, however much I have said, it is useless; I cannot get out of your minds [the idea] that in that sacrament, sitting there, there is not a man, but rather, I know, Jesus Christ, ready with his wounds open to wash your soul. How sorry I am about this, and how great a sorrow I bear at seeing you take so little account of it! Very different should be the thought you have of it, and very different the preparation you should make. Daughters, let me tell you what your mind is doing while you make your examination: it is thinking of things quite different from your sins. If you had a sensitive heart, it would throb with sorrow and love for having offended your Jesus, the One who sustains you every day and gives you so many graces.

Tell me, if you had a friend whom you loved with all your heart, and you offended her and upset her, would you not feel your heart torn with sorrow? Isn't that so?

“In anger I let myself be carried to excess, by which I opened that wound which is streaming with blood in the heart of our Jesus.” I have wanted to compare this sorrow of Jesus to a person's human affection. If we are so small that we do not know how to make our examination, if we thought like this, what our sorrow would be! What pain you would feel tearing your heart at these thoughts! Ah, it seems that the mouth of Jesus, those open wounds, say to me: if you wish, I have prepared for you the very [remedy] to heal my wounds; the torment is in your soul, which you have despised, and which is now degraded within you.

But I have prepared a bath to purify it. Ah, daughters, let us not be like the pool of Bethesda, where many went in but few were those whom the Angel came down to purify; for you, [he] has opened [the fountain] continually to wash you, to purify you. Only God and your Guardian Angel know it, who covers his face with his wings so as not to see how little account you take of this sacrament. Ah, I seem to hear that voice crying: what shall I say of those who take so little account of my Most Precious Blood? How many times they commit sacrileges!… Ah, daughters, how many examples I could tell you about those who went to receive this sacrament, to make you know the power it has! Of Saint Philip Neri we know that many went to him to mock this sacrament and this saint, and while they confessed in jest, he, enlightened by God and seeing those hearts, would begin to weep, so that the penitent, struck with compunction, ended up weeping too, and then was converted…

Daughters, that Blood washes away your sins. Ah, if I could instill one thought in your souls: that in that sacrament you are washed with the Blood of Jesus Christ, that in that Red Sea your soul becomes beautiful, pure and dear to your Jesus! Daughters, rather stop going to confession than go and commit a sacrilege. My God, those acts of disobedience, that obstinacy in that sin! Enough, I will go no further; the one whose heart is pounding will hear it well, and whoever has a stained conscience will understand me. It is impossible, daughters: you will never enjoy the peace the soul feels when united with God until you are better. Believe me, daughters, once that priest has heard your sins he knows nothing more and forgets everything instantly. You know that the seal of confession cannot be revealed; the confessor cannot say a word about his penitents; believe me, it cannot happen and never will happen that a confessor has said anything about his penitent… Do you know what the saints did when they approached this sacrament? They tasted that most sweet nectar, they were set on fire with the love of God, and how many graces God poured into their souls, by which they rose to the greatest perfection! And you eat the bread without tasting it…

Know that while the priest raises his hand to give you absolution, after the words he pronounces your sins are wiped out, even those you may have forgotten through inadvertence; and after receiving absolution you must not think of them any more, but, humbled and recollected within yourselves, say and repeat several times: my God, mercy.

Yes, my daughters, at the moment the priest raises his hands you must humble yourselves and repeat: my God, mercy. Divine Blood that comes down to wash my soul, yes, wash it with your grace. And our soul, doing this, will be beautiful and clean of every sin. My daughters, think now whether you do this. If you thought like this, what absolution you would receive, and what desire you would have! To go to confession as often as possible. Ah yes, I would go every day if I could, and what joy it would be for me to make my soul more beautiful and pure of every sin, of every stain! Instead you let the teacher drag you along, saying: this blessed confessor is always here!…

I want to hope that you will mend your ways and want to put an end once and for all to this bad behavior of yours.

… O our holy Mother Saint Anne, you who are so powerful in heaven, turn a look of pity and mercy on these creatures. Dear Mother, Mary, for charity's sake, grant that none of these creatures may fall into a bad life, may be lost; heal their souls and assure them of Paradise.

To the girls of Piacenza (boarders) — January 1871

Let us accompany, O my daughters, our Child on this journey from Bethlehem to Egypt. Ah, how much he suffers, for whoever travels cannot help suffering! And who is traveling? It is the King of heaven and earth, the Son of God.

My Child, did you need to set out on a journey in this cold season, without swaddling clothes, and in such cold? And you, O Mary, O Immaculate, O beautiful Mary, so delicate, so young, you who descended from royal stock, I can imagine what pain your tender feet, unused to walking so far, will feel. Ah, if we turn to the third person, we shudder to see him without his cloak, which he had taken from his bent shoulders to cover the King of Heaven, carrying on his own shoulders the provisions, under whose weight it seems to me he must give way at any moment. How can I, wretched creature, keep silent at this sight, seeing these great persons hurrying along so resigned? And where are they going? To hide the Child Jesus.

Oh, dear little virgin Mary, how anxious your heart is as you hold the Child in your arms! Ah yes, Mary could well tell me that the Child Jesus did not become heavy, as the children of men are heavy; but she carried him joyfully, and he filled her with holy gladness.

Ah yes, my daughters, whoever has Jesus in her heart never feels anything heavy or painful, and we can always have him, by his great mercy. He is always calling us with those delicate little hands from that Tabernacle to enter our hearts, and he wants nothing but to come and dwell in them. Ah yes, with Jesus in our heart we shall feel neither pain nor sorrow. But what am I saying, my God? It is quite true that the soul that receives you finds nothing but relief for its sufferings; yes, there can be no other joy than when Jesus is in our heart. Ah yes, he alone can give resignation in our ills, in our sufferings; he alone can give our heart that peace, that consolation the world cannot give. If we look at the people of the world, we see them restless in themselves, and why? Because they find no peace in their pleasures; sunk in their passions, they have not a moment's respite. On the contrary, blessed is the soul that has Jesus in her heart: he gives her peace, consolation, that unchanging calm even in the midst of the fiercest battles she may have with the world. He gives her resignation in her sufferings. “My God,” she says, “what do I know? I know that you will one day reward me for this suffering with your glory, for I know that without crosses and trials one does not enter heaven. Your dwelling, O my God, is the reward of those who suffer the ills of this world with peace and resignation”; and this thought revives and spurs her to suffer. “Yes, I have this sorrow that gives me no peace, I cannot sleep.” Well then, she hears an inner voice from her Jesus saying to her: this sorrow I send you will one day be of greater glory. The worldly soul, instead, its mind filled with so many worldly thoughts, impure thoughts, earthly thoughts, will build castle upon castle, and in the end finds itself weary and has nothing but smoke; and these thoughts serve only to draw it away from God and weaken the mind. How often it happens to so many young girls who think of nothing but reaching the goal they have set themselves, and then time destroys that worldly taste, that pleasure, and they find they have nothing.

Ah, think seriously, O my daughters, that a day will come when you will set foot in that world which is nothing but appearance; your worldly sojourn, know it, will end, death will come and you will find you have nothing for eternity. O my God, with your strength keep firm in the hearts of these daughters of yours all that your holy religion commands. Your body, if you use it to please the world, will become nothing but a corpse, with no more hope of coming back to life.

Our actions, know it, are what must lead us to an eternity of joy or an eternity of torment. Yes, this earth will soon pass away and eternity will take its place. Always keep our God before your eyes and say to him often: yes, O my Jesus, if I have loved you, you will be father and spouse to me; if I have carried you in my breast like the Virgin Mary, the eternal Father will open his right hand to me, and I shall not have to see Jesus as judge but as the spouse who will lead me to joy for an eternity. How many of those worldly souls I have seen die! Ah, daughters, what a difference there is between a virgin and a worldly bride!

… But you will say to me: Mother, you say this because we are following in your footsteps. Ah no, they are the very footsteps of the Gospel, which I have had to touch with my own hands so many times; and all I have told you, to return to the meditation, is true: Jesus relieves your sufferings. It is true that Jesus does not call everyone to be Saints, to be martyrs, but he calls everyone to keep his commandments; it is enough that the wife keeps them well: she is the virgin that Jesus wants, that holy Church wants.

Oh, blessed is she who can say: I have spent my life for my Jesus! Blessed is she; the bundle she will carry with her for an eternity will be hers. All she does, she does for herself; all the virtues she practices are for herself. It is true, daughter, that the soul who acts like this can be called a miser who heaps up treasures for eternal life, and that soul is a sovereign because she has found a sovereign spouse. When I think of a young girl who has become a spouse of Jesus, how many thoughts crowd into my mind, and how my soul rejoices!

You will say: these things are not for us, they are for religious. Ah, daughters, how many there are in the world who, unable to become religious through poor health or some other reason, live in their homes with their families, of which they are the angels, giving the world shining examples of virtue. Ah, my daughters, you too can do this, living in your families: you can be the peace, the consolation, the good example of everyone by your charity; you can sweeten the troubles of your neighbors and of the unfortunate. Always try, O daughters, by your humility to sweeten everyone's troubles, especially those of your family, in every situation in which we may find ourselves. Then let us look at that Child who was king of heaven and earth and became poor, often without even a crust of bread. When we find ourselves lacking something, let us think of Jesus who as a Child helped Saint Joseph in his labors, and after working all day often had nowhere to rest his sacred little body.

Weigh this well; do not let yourselves be deceived by those spirits of hell who with their talk do nothing but confuse your souls and make them perish forever. Ah, they are nothing but spirits of hell who feel nothing and have a heart only for the world…

O daughters, you will have to enter that world, you will have to hear the words of those barbarians who, to find peace for their troubled consciences, will try with their words to draw you to their side. Like the devil, they are convinced; they know they are on a bad road, and so they try to draw others onto it too. For charity's sake, stand firm in your holy religion. They will tell you that only the pious women and the nuns will be saved, but you will answer them that Jesus Christ left it written: many are called but few are chosen.

Saint Teresa, to whom God had granted to see where the souls of the dying went, saw them falling into hell like falling snow. And we, who by the mercy of God have been chosen, it depends on us alone to respond to so great a grace. Those lazy people will tell you that kneeling so long will tire you and harm you. Ah no, let us never listen to them; let us rather increase our prayers and think often of paradise, of Jesus. My daughters, a woman who has these thoughts in her heart enjoys a foretaste of paradise, for her family is like the house of Saint Joachim. But very different will be the house of the woman who goes about thoughtlessly, squandering, thinking only of enjoying herself. I have often spoken to you of those young virgins who go about and live in the world like little angels; I have shown you that it is they who hold back the arm of the Almighty, angered by the sins of men. It is said that the prayers of virgins rising to God are answered, if not one day then another. The virgin who speaks to her Jesus and says to him: my Jesus, I want, I need this grace — for a while Jesus turns a deaf ear and lets her pray, but in the end, seeing that she keeps on knocking without ever tiring, that she is trusting, he always hears her and grants her everything.

… And you, O Blessed Virgin, O Immaculate Mary, do not allow these creatures of yours to be defiled by that ugly sin. You are the protection of youth. Ah, open your mantle, so that our eyes may see nothing but the beauties of heaven, and our ears hear nothing but the harmonious song of your angels. Ah, for charity's sake, may they never have to come out from under your motherly mantle.

Saint Anne, our Mother, sovereign protectress, be always our support in our steps, our strength in our battles, our guide to the gate of heaven.

To the girls of Piacenza — January 1870

Here we are in your divine presence, O almighty God. If only one knew how to raise the human mind to contemplate you! Certainly, while in your presence the whole person would take the attitude due to so great a sovereign as you, my God, king of heaven and earth. And I, poor creature, am not able to raise my mind to that majesty in heaven which all the Blessed enjoy, being inebriated by the bliss of your presence and feeding on it!

This thought should be enough to know how beautiful the majesty of God is. Your throne is of a power without equal, for in you is the delight of that blessed dwelling of the Seraphim. And how is it that I, poor girl, did not even know that I was before you, O my Sovereign!

I used to go to the church where Jesus your Son dwells, and as if forgetful of everything, almost as if I were in a room, I would sit down without making a genuflection. Ah, daughters, and why did I say: they come to tell you that you are my Father who lives in heaven? What boldness, O daughters, that, young and strong as you are, you have not been able to bend the knee a little! Were you perhaps afraid of hurting yourself?

Ah, my Jesus, grant that from now on my knee may know how to bend, and that this mind, my God, which has been able to think only of vain, frivolous, impure things, may turn to you, and at least in that little time I spend in your divine presence may adore you.

Oh, we must indeed say that the girl who slouches in church and does not kneel up straight, let us say it, O daughters, has never made a meditation. For if she made even a little, all compunction before her God, on entering the church she would know how to adore the sovereign of sovereigns, the king of kings, with her forehead on the ground. Instead, a little noise at the door, someone coming in or going out, and there we are at once turning our eyes to see who is coming, even at those moments, my God, when I am preparing to receive my God, the sovereign of Paradise, in a little while! At that moment, O my God, the Saints trembled, after preparing for three days beforehand, as Saint Aloysius Gonzaga did. Ah, daughters, do you know whom we receive? That God who has given you so many graces, who washed you in holy baptism, who took you out of the sin in which you were steeped, a grace he did not give to so many others who live on this earth like animals, and who wants nothing but to enter your soul, all love, to sanctify you and take his delight in you.

Ah, Jesus, here we are all full of compunction, humbled in your presence; I bend my knee, my forehead, I try to draw from this that union with you, O my God, before receiving you. Ah, purify me, cast a look of mercy on my soul and make it less foul, make it beautiful, before you come to dwell in it.

Eternal Father, I am preparing to receive that divine Jesus whom I myself have flayed, pierced and put on the cross with my sins; I have despised his Humanity. Here I am now before you, full of shame; I throw myself at your most holy feet, I go there to drink my fill of those wounds, and behold, I enter the wound of your sacred shoulder. My Eternal Father, my dear God, look upon this wound of my Jesus opened by the heaviest cross. O dear Jesus, why so much suffering? I myself was the one who so often reopened it, making you carry the cross of my sins. You called me so many times, you said to me: beloved spouse, have you the heart to make me suffer so cruelly? Ah, stop it, stop it, stop it once and for all; you lay on me a weight that flays my bones and throws me to the ground. How cruel you are!

Ah, my dear Jesus, do not speak to me like this any more, I beg you; give me this cross, I will clasp it as a pledge of your love. My beloved cross, I will carry you, not on my shoulders like my Jesus, for I am unworthy of it, but on my breast, so that you may show that my Jesus is in this breast. At this sign all hell will tremble and those evil spirits will no longer be able to come near. But what am I saying? I was already imagining I had my Jesus within me, while I have not yet thought of cleaning this little room of mine? Ah, my God, what will you say on entering it? Ah, only your mercy will be able to wash everything, to clean everything.

Ah, my daughters, from this wound I can have every good. Yes, my Jesus, I clasp you and with my tongue I will drink all the blood that flows from it and wash my soul with it (…) You are a delightful banquet; if you found my breast prepared as you desire, you would feed me and fill me. Ah, my Good, shall I have the heart, the nerve, not to have holy thoughts, not to have my mind wholly for you? The saints were right to cry out: ah, my Love, enough, enough, too much, too much joy you give me! Ah, my Love, what are you doing?

My daughters, this is what the Saints did: they thought that they had within them the one love of their souls. They had sweet words to say to their Jesus. What fire there was in them! What love they nourished in their breasts! Ah, why is my heart so cold? Ah, why have I never had the honor of bringing my lips close to your wounds? You opened them to me to give me heaven, which can be had only from you. Ah, how many blessed virgins, on approaching the table of their Jesus, felt a joy that no human mind or tongue can describe! A Saint Francis of Paola used to say on approaching the holy table that the sweetness he felt was so great that he cried out: My God Charity, my God Charity, I am dying! (…) And when shall we stop keeping this little room closed, and why shall we not let him pour himself into it and spread his graces, for he washes and leaves the soul beautiful; and why do you seek only to defile it?

Ah yes, my God, and when shall I stop committing so many acts of disobedience, so many Communions made so badly? Ah, we are without charity. Ah, daughters, and when shall we have the charity those holy young virgins had, whom the Lord did not know how to load enough with his graces? Ah yes, let us make firm resolutions; let the first be to see that our knee always bends in the presence of God. I will gather the powers of my intellect and pray this divine majesty to set his foot on my head, so that I may be in church as so many Saints were, who on entering the church always kept their forehead on the ground. But, my Jesus, in a little while I shall receive you. Mary, my Mother, mother of my Jesus, ah, do not allow your divine Son to come to me unless first, with your most holy hands, you prepare this poor little room. Adorn it, enrich it, make it fit to receive your Sovereign Son.

To the girls of Piacenza — January 28, 1871

… Daughters, this Father sustains us with such charity, provides us with every means for our sanctification, gave us his only-begotten divine Son who by his passion gave us this cross still enameled with his most precious Blood. Ah, daughters, blessed will be the soul that has run her life in this vale of tears under it! Ah, one day you will see it with those holes still sending out rays of that most pure Blood of Jesus. My God, you have sanctified this blessed cross with your immense love; one day we shall see it all radiant with rubies, and we shall see blessed the creature who knew how to love it.

You will say to me: she can tell us nothing but crosses, she speaks to us of nothing but a road of mortification. But, my daughters, what am I to tell you? I will speak to you only of things I know, and if you put them into practice they will lead you to be eternally happy, as I would like one day to see you all; for God knows how much I love you, so that I would give all my blood for you. Of your souls, you see, and of all of you, from the first to the very last, I am and shall be as jealous as of the pupil of my eye until the last moment of my life. Ah, my daughters, would I point out to you a road that would lead you to the cruelest torments and to sufferings for an eternity? Ah, if that were so, if I had to see such a sight, O my Eternal Father, you can change it and make of all hearts so many chosen vessels. Daughters, believe that the way of the cross is not the one that will break your heart; rather you will feel in it a consolation that is not vain and deceptive like that brought by the pleasures of this earth, which break the heart and leave the soul full of sorrows for an eternity. That is why I am always pointing out to you the way of the cross; I encourage you to carry it, not as they do in the world, carrying it and then throwing it to the ground, only to be led to an eternity of hell. Ah, my daughters, you who are to go into a world where the cross is mocked and despised! Woe to you, O daughter, if you have not been able to free yourself from those diabolical suggestions with which those evil spirits of the world incited you.

To the Sisters of Ferrara, 4.7.18…

The Lord has given me twenty, thirty girls to look after; well then, I want them to become good and dear to God; a day will come when they will be religious.

Ah, these little girls, how rough and naughty they are! We cannot say so, for whoever loves God must try to make all these hearts love God. If these hearts have grown up without knowing God, in the mud of the earth, well then, let us turn these hearts around by winning them for God, let us cleanse them with our care, so that the creature will love her God, come out of her lethargy and begin to live in God. Yes, because whoever has understanding loves God. The teacher must win the hearts of all the children. If I do not so capture the hearts of all the little girls that when they leave school they say: ah, come to my school, here one comes to know God and enjoys a peace never known before, there is a teacher who wins every heart!

You see, I tell you these things because I have experienced them. I had a Parish in my charge and they all loved me. You will say to me: but at Ferrara they are naughty, they have never had a father or a mother. Enough, they have a heart: steal it from them and you will be able to do what you like with them. Do not do this so that the little girls will love me, no, for God's sake. Jesus, say to him, I give you this heart that I have stolen for you, which loves you and knows you; yes, steal their hearts and you will do what you like with them. Yes, try to steal their hearts for God. What a sorrow at the last judgment to think: how many hearts I could have given to Jesus, and instead how many have been lost through my fault! You must attract them with gentleness, for bees are caught with honey.
